Represents the 'maxp' (maximum profile) table with various upper bounds used during TrueType hinting and loading, such as max points, contours, and instruction sizes.

functions.name: FT_Init_FreeType
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Init_FreeType( FT_Library *alibrary );
functions.description: Initializes a new FreeType library object and registers the default set of modules. Use to begin using the FreeType API.
requirements: alibrary must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created FT_Library handle
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure
If custom memory management or reference-counting is needed, prefer FT_New_Library/FT_Done_Library instead
In multi-threaded use, creating and destroying faces sharing the same library must be serialized (per library doc notes)

functions.name: FT_Done_FreeType
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Done_FreeType( FT_Library library );
functions.description: Destroys a FreeType library object and all child objects (faces, sizes, resources, drivers).
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library obtained from FT_Init_FreeType or FT_New_Library
All faces/sizes created from this library become invalid after this call
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_New_Face
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_New_Face( FT_Library library, const char* filepathname, FT_Long face_index, FT_Face *aface );
functions.description: Opens a font file by path and creates an FT_Face. This is a convenience wrapper around FT_Open_Face with pathname.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library
filepathname must point to a C string path (no embedded null bytes except terminator) recognizable by fopen on the platform
aface must be non-NULL if face_index >= 0 to receive the FT_Face
face_index selects face and optionally named instance as defined by FT_Open_Face
Use FT_Done_Face to destroy the returned FT_Face
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_New_Memory_Face
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_New_Memory_Face( FT_Library library, const FT_Byte* file_base, FT_Long file_size, FT_Long face_index, FT_Face *aface );
functions.description: Opens a font from a memory buffer and creates an FT_Face. Wrapper around FT_Open_Face for memory data.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library
file_base must point to the beginning of the font data buffer; file_size is its size in bytes
Caller must keep the memory buffer alive until after FT_Done_Face is called on the created face
aface must be non-NULL if face_index >= 0 to receive the FT_Face
face_index selects face and optionally named instance as defined by FT_Open_Face
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Open_Face
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Open_Face( FT_Library library, const FT_Open_Args* args, FT_Long face_index, FT_Face *aface );
functions.description: Creates an FT_Face from a resource described by FT_Open_Args (memory, stream, or pathname). Supports selecting faces and named instances.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library
args must point to a properly initialized FT_Open_Args; the combination of FT_OPEN_MEMORY, FT_OPEN_STREAM, and FT_OPEN_PATHNAME flags must be valid (mutually exclusive); otherwise call fails
If FT_OPEN_DRIVER is set, args->driver must be set
If FT_OPEN_PARAMS is set, args->num_params and args->params must be set
When FT_OPEN_STREAM is set and an error occurs, the stream is automatically closed before return
aface must be non-NULL if face_index >= 0 to receive the FT_Face
Negative face_index values are allowed for probing; if used, the returned face (if any) must be destroyed with FT_Done_Face after inspection
Multiple faces can be opened from a single FT_Library
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Attach_File
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Attach_File( FT_Face face, const char* filepathname );
functions.description: Attaches auxiliary data to a face from an external file (e.g., AFM for Type 1 kerning). Convenience wrapper around FT_Attach_Stream for pathnames.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
filepathname must be a valid C string path
Attachment behavior is driver/format-specific; many drivers do not implement attachments
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Attach_Stream
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Attach_Stream( FT_Face face, const FT_Open_Args* parameters );
functions.description: Attaches auxiliary data to a face using an FT_Open_Args-described stream (e.g., for AFM kerning).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
parameters must point to a valid FT_Open_Args describing the attachment data source
Attachment semantics are driver/format-specific; many drivers do not implement attachments
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Reference_Face
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Reference_Face( FT_Face face );
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an FT_Face. FT_Done_Face will only destroy the face when the count reaches 1 then decrement to 0.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Use to manage shared ownership of faces across components/threads
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Done_Face
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Done_Face( FT_Face face );
functions.description: Destroys a face object and all associated slots and sizes if its reference count reaches zero.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face (or NULL for a no-op is unspecified; treat as must be valid)
Respect reference counting as established by FT_Reference_Face
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Select_Size
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Select_Size( FT_Face face, FT_Int strike_index );
functions.description: Selects a bitmap strike by setting the active FT_Size scaling to match the strike at the given index.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
strike_index must be a valid index into face->available_sizes (0..face->num_fixed_sizes-1)
Only meaningful for faces with embedded bitmaps; outlines are used if a glyph lacks a bitmap at that strike
Bitmap strikes are ignored for non-default variation instances
Do not use with the FreeType cache API
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Request_Size
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Request_Size( FT_Face face, FT_Size_Request req );
functions.description: Resizes the scale of the active FT_Size according to the provided size request (points, pixels, bbox, cell, or direct scales).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
req must point to a valid FT_Size_RequestRec describing the request
Drivers may or may not select a bitmap strike; use FT_Select_Size to choose a specific strike
Zero width or height semantics differ from FT_Set_Char_Size; zero values are treated as FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE here
Do not use with the FreeType cache API
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Char_Size
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_Char_Size( FT_Face face, FT_F26Dot6 char_width, FT_F26Dot6 char_height, FT_UInt horz_resolution, FT_UInt vert_resolution );
functions.description: Requests the nominal character size in 26.6 fractional points at given resolutions. Wrapper over FT_Request_Size for nominal type.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
char_width and char_height are 26.6 point values; if one is zero, it is set to the other
horz_resolution and vert_resolution are in dpi; if one is zero, it is set to the other
Widths/heights < 1pt are set to 1pt; if both resolutions are zero, they default to 72 dpi
Resulting ppem are rounded to nearest integer
Do not use with the FreeType cache API
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes( FT_Face face, FT_UInt pixel_width, FT_UInt pixel_height );
functions.description: Requests the nominal character size in pixels. Wrapper over FT_Request_Size for pixel sizing.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
pixel_width and pixel_height are nominal pixel dimensions; actual glyph sizes may differ per font design
Do not use with the FreeType cache API
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Load_Glyph
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Load_Glyph( FT_Face face, FT_UInt glyph_index, FT_Int32 load_flags );
functions.description: Loads a glyph by index into the face's glyph slot, scaling and hinting according to the active size and load flags.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face; its active FT_Size should be meaningfully initialized for proper scaling/hinting
glyph_index is the glyph index (or CID for subsetted CID-keyed fonts); invalid CID in subsetted CID-keyed fonts yields FT_Err_Invalid_Argument
load_flags is a combination of FT_LOAD_XXX values; certain flags imply others as documented
If FT_LOAD_RENDER is set, the glyph is rendered after loading
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure (e.g., FT_Err_Glyph_Too_Big)

functions.name: FT_Load_Char
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Load_Char( FT_Face face, FT_ULong char_code, FT_Int32 load_flags );
functions.description: Loads a glyph by character code via the current charmap, then loads that glyph into the glyph slot (equivalent to FT_Get_Char_Index + FT_Load_Glyph).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
face->charmap should be set to a valid charmap; if no active charmap, behaves like FT_Load_Glyph using char_code as index
load_flags is a combination of FT_LOAD_XXX values
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Transform
functions.signature: void FT_Set_Transform( FT_Face face, FT_Matrix* matrix, FT_Vector* delta );
functions.description: Sets a 2x2 transformation matrix and translation vector applied to scalable glyph images when they are loaded.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
matrix may be NULL for identity; delta may be NULL for zero translation
Transformation is applied after glyph loading and does not affect hinting; it affects face->glyph.advance but not face->glyph.metrics
FT_Matrix uses 16.16 fixed-point; precision is limited

functions.name: FT_Get_Transform
functions.signature: void FT_Get_Transform( FT_Face face, FT_Matrix* matrix, FT_Vector* delta );
functions.description: Returns the current transform matrix and translation vector applied on glyph load, as set by FT_Set_Transform.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
matrix may be NULL if the caller is not interested; delta may be NULL if not interested

functions.name: FT_Render_Glyph
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Render_Glyph( FT_GlyphSlot slot, FT_Render_Mode render_mode );
functions.description: Converts the glyph image in a glyph slot to a bitmap using the given render mode, selecting an appropriate renderer.
requirements: slot must be a valid FT_GlyphSlot with a loaded glyph image
render_mode must be a valid FT_Render_Mode
If render mode is FT_RENDER_MODE_NORMAL and the glyph has color layers with FT_LOAD_COLOR used earlier, default blending may occur (experimental, v0 COLR only)
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure
Output bitmap is an alpha coverage map; correct compositing requires linear blending as documented

functions.name: FT_Get_Kerning
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Kerning( FT_Face face, FT_UInt left_glyph, FT_UInt right_glyph, FT_UInt kern_mode, FT_Vector *akerning );
functions.description: Returns the kerning vector between two glyph indices for the given face and kerning mode.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
left_glyph and right_glyph are glyph indices
kern_mode must be one of FT_Kerning_Mode values
akerning must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the kerning vector
Only horizontal layouts are supported by this API
FreeType may use 'kern' table and basic GPOS pair kerning (if enabled); 'kern' table takes precedence
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_Track_Kerning
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Track_Kerning( FT_Face face, FT_Fixed point_size, FT_Int degree, FT_Fixed* akerning );
functions.description: Returns uniform track kerning for a given face at a given 16.16 point size and degree of tightness.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
akerning must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the kerning in 16.16 points
Only the Type 1 driver supports track kerning via AFM files; an AFM must be attached via FT_Attach_File/FT_Attach_Stream for data to be available
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Select_Charmap
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Select_Charmap( FT_Face face, FT_Encoding encoding );
functions.description: Selects a charmap in the face by encoding tag, preferring the best Unicode cmap if multiple are present.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
encoding must be a valid FT_Encoding tag
Returns an error if no matching charmap exists in the face
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Charmap
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_Charmap( FT_Face face, FT_CharMap charmap );
functions.description: Sets the active charmap for character code to glyph index mapping.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
charmap must be a charmap that belongs to the face (present in face->charmaps)
Fails if an OpenType type 14 (format 14) charmap is selected
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_Charmap_Index
functions.signature: FT_Int FT_Get_Charmap_Index( FT_CharMap charmap );
functions.description: Retrieves the index of the given charmap within its parent face's charmap array.
requirements: charmap must be a valid FT_CharMap
Returns -1 on error

functions.name: FT_Get_Char_Index
functions.signature: FT_UInt FT_Get_Char_Index( FT_Face face, FT_ULong charcode );
functions.description: Returns the glyph index corresponding to a character code per the current active charmap.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
charcode is the character code in the active encoding
Returns 0 if the character code is undefined
Be aware glyph index 0 is reserved for the missing glyph; FreeType may remap indices internally to ensure this

functions.name: FT_Get_First_Char
functions.signature: FT_ULong FT_Get_First_Char( FT_Face face, FT_UInt *agindex );
functions.description: Returns the first character code in the current charmap along with its glyph index.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
agindex must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the glyph index (0 if the charmap is empty)
May return 0 either because the charmap is empty or because 0 is the first valid code
Character codes can be up to 0xFFFFFFFF; iterating may be large for certain cmaps

functions.name: FT_Get_Next_Char
functions.signature: FT_ULong FT_Get_Next_Char( FT_Face face, FT_ULong char_code, FT_UInt *agindex );
functions.description: Returns the next character code after char_code in the current charmap, and its glyph index.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
agindex must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the glyph index
Sets *agindex to 0 when there are no more codes

functions.name: FT_Face_Properties
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Face_Properties( FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_properties, FT_Parameter* properties );
functions.description: Sets or overrides certain library/module properties on a per-face basis using an array of FT_Parameter entries.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
properties must point to an array of num_properties FT_Parameter elements
Only specific tags are supported: FT_PARAM_TAG_STEM_DARKENING, FT_PARAM_TAG_LCD_FILTER_WEIGHTS, FT_PARAM_TAG_RANDOM_SEED
To reset a property to default, pass the tag with data = NULL
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_Name_Index
functions.signature: FT_UInt FT_Get_Name_Index( FT_Face face, const FT_String* glyph_name );
functions.description: Returns the glyph index for a given ASCII glyph name, if the face provides glyph names.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
glyph_name must be a valid pointer to a zero-terminated ASCII name
Works only if FT_HAS_GLYPH_NAMES(face) is true; limited capability if FT_CONFIG_OPTION_POSTSCRIPT_NAMES is not defined
Returns 0 if the name is undefined

functions.name: FT_Get_Glyph_Name
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Glyph_Name( FT_Face face, FT_UInt glyph_index, FT_Pointer buffer, FT_UInt buffer_max );
functions.description: Retrieves the ASCII glyph name for a given glyph index, if available.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
buffer must point to writable memory of at least buffer_max bytes
buffer_max is the maximum number of bytes; output is zero-terminated and truncated if necessary
Returns an error if the face has no glyph names or glyph_index is invalid; on failure, buffer[0] is set to 0
Limited capability if FT_CONFIG_OPTION_POSTSCRIPT_NAMES is not defined

functions.name: FT_Get_Postscript_Name
functions.signature: const char* FT_Get_Postscript_Name( FT_Face face );
functions.description: Returns the ASCII PostScript name of the given face, if available (PS, TrueType, OpenType).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Return value is owned by the face and becomes invalid when the face is destroyed
For variation fonts, the returned string can change with the selected instance; call again after changing instance
May return NULL if unavailable

functions.name: FT_Get_SubGlyph_Info
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_SubGlyph_Info( FT_GlyphSlot glyph, FT_UInt sub_index, FT_Int *p_index, FT_UInt *p_flags, FT_Int *p_arg1, FT_Int *p_arg2, FT_Matrix *p_transform );
functions.description: Retrieves description data for a subglyph of a composite glyph in a glyph slot.
requirements: glyph must be a valid FT_GlyphSlot with glyph->format == FT_GLYPH_FORMAT_COMPOSITE; otherwise an error is returned
sub_index must be less than glyph->num_subglyphs
p_index, p_flags, p_arg1, p_arg2, and p_transform must be valid pointers if the corresponding data is desired
Interpretation of args and transform depends on flags per OpenType 'glyf' composite description
Returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_FSType_Flags
functions.signature: FT_UShort FT_Get_FSType_Flags( FT_Face face );
functions.description: Returns embedding and subsetting permission flags (fsType/FSType) for the font as FT_FSTYPE_XXX bits.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Use this API instead of reading PS_FontInfoRec fs_type directly (only reliable for Type 1 faces)

functions.name: FT_Face_GetCharVariantIndex
functions.signature: FT_UInt FT_Face_GetCharVariantIndex( FT_Face face, FT_ULong charcode, FT_ULong variantSelector );
functions.description: Returns the glyph index for a Unicode character modified by a variation selector (cmap format 14).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Meaningful only if the face has a variation selector cmap subtable and the current charmap is Unicode
Returns 0 if undefined character/selector, no format 14 cmap, or current charmap is not Unicode

functions.name: FT_Face_GetCharVariantIsDefault
functions.signature: FT_Int FT_Face_GetCharVariantIsDefault( FT_Face face, FT_ULong charcode, FT_ULong variantSelector );
functions.description: Checks whether the specified variation of a Unicode character is the default glyph in the standard Unicode cmap.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Returns 1 if found in the standard Unicode cmap, 0 if found in the variation selector cmap, or -1 if not a variation
Meaningful only if the face has a variation selector cmap subtable

functions.name: FT_Face_GetVariantSelectors
functions.signature: FT_UInt32* FT_Face_GetVariantSelectors( FT_Face face );
functions.description: Returns a zero-terminated array of Unicode variation selector code points present in the font (from cmap format 14).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Returned array is owned by the FT_Face and may be overwritten or released on the next FreeType call
Returns NULL if no valid variation selector cmap subtable

functions.name: FT_Face_GetVariantsOfChar
functions.signature: FT_UInt32* FT_Face_GetVariantsOfChar( FT_Face face, FT_ULong charcode );
functions.description: Returns a zero-terminated array of variation selector code points active for the given Unicode character.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Returned array is owned by the FT_Face and may be overwritten or released on the next FreeType call
Returns NULL if the list is empty

functions.name: FT_Face_GetCharsOfVariant
functions.signature: FT_UInt32* FT_Face_GetCharsOfVariant( FT_Face face, FT_ULong variantSelector );
functions.description: Returns a zero-terminated array of Unicode characters that have entries for the specified variation selector.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
Returned array is owned by the FT_Face and may be overwritten or released on the next FreeType call
Returns NULL if there is no valid cmap or the selector is invalid

functions.name: FT_MulDiv
functions.signature: FT_Long FT_MulDiv( FT_Long a, FT_Long b, FT_Long c );
functions.description: Computes (a*b)/c with maximum accuracy using a 64-bit intermediate when necessary; portable helper.
requirements: Valid integer inputs expected; division by zero does not trap and returns MaxInt or MinInt depending on signs of a and b

functions.name: FT_MulFix
functions.signature: FT_Long FT_MulFix( FT_Long a, FT_Long b );
functions.description: Computes (a*b)/0x10000 accurately. Used to multiply by a 16.16 fixed-point factor.
requirements: b should be a 16.16 factor for optimal use; function is optimized when |a| < 2048 and b is 16.16

functions.name: FT_DivFix
functions.signature: FT_Long FT_DivFix( FT_Long a, FT_Long b );
functions.description: Computes (a*0x10000)/b accurately. Used to divide by a 16.16 fixed-point factor.
requirements: b is the denominator and should be a 16.16 factor

functions.name: FT_RoundFix
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_RoundFix( FT_Fixed a );
functions.description: Rounds a 16.16 fixed-point number to the nearest integer (16.16), half away from zero.
requirements: Uses wrap-around arithmetic; input must be a 16.16 fixed-point value

functions.name: FT_CeilFix
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_CeilFix( FT_Fixed a );
functions.description: Computes the ceiling of a 16.16 fixed-point number (smallest following integer in 16.16).
requirements: Uses wrap-around arithmetic; input must be a 16.16 fixed-point value

functions.name: FT_FloorFix
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_FloorFix( FT_Fixed a );
functions.description: Computes the floor of a 16.16 fixed-point number (largest previous integer in 16.16).
requirements: Input must be a 16.16 fixed-point value

functions.name: FT_Vector_Transform
functions.signature: void FT_Vector_Transform( FT_Vector* vector, const FT_Matrix* matrix );
functions.description: Transforms a single vector by a 2x2 matrix.
requirements: vector must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an FT_Vector to be transformed
matrix must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an FT_Matrix; result is undefined if either argument is invalid

functions.name: FT_Library_Version
functions.signature: void FT_Library_Version( FT_Library library, FT_Int *amajor, FT_Int *aminor, FT_Int *apatch );
functions.description: Returns the version numbers (major, minor, patch) of the FreeType library in use.
requirements: library should be a valid FT_Library; may be required if the program didn't use FT_Init_FreeType for custom initialization
amajor, aminor, and apatch are output pointers; any may be NULL if the caller is not interested in that value

functions.name: FT_Face_CheckTrueTypePatents
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Face_CheckTrueTypePatents( FT_Face face );
functions.description: Deprecated; does nothing. Always returns false. TrueType hinting is no longer patented.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face

functions.name: FT_Face_SetUnpatentedHinting
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Face_SetUnpatentedHinting( FT_Face face, FT_Bool value );
functions.description: Deprecated; does nothing. Always returns false. TrueType hinting is no longer patented.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face

functions.name: FT_New_Glyph
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Error ) FT_New_Glyph( FT_Library       library, FT_Glyph_Format  format, FT_Glyph         *aglyph );
functions.description: Create a new empty FT_Glyph object of the given image format. The resulting glyph must later be released with FT_Done_Glyph. Typical usage is to allocate a glyph container prior to populating it or transforming it.
requirements: library must be a valid, initialized FT_Library handle.
aglyph must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created FT_Glyph handle.
On success the caller owns the returned glyph and must release it with FT_Done_Glyph.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Get_Glyph
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Error ) FT_Get_Glyph( FT_GlyphSlot  slot, FT_Glyph     *aglyph );
functions.description: Extract a glyph image from an FT_GlyphSlot into a standalone FT_Glyph object detached from the face/slot. The created glyph must be freed with FT_Done_Glyph. Commonly used after FT_Load_Glyph/FT_Load_Char to retain a glyph image.
requirements: slot must be a valid FT_GlyphSlot with a glyph already loaded (e.g., via FT_Load_Glyph/FT_Load_Char).
aglyph must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new FT_Glyph; it is set to NULL on error.
Because the resulting FT_Glyph advance is 16.16, slot->advance.x and slot->advance.y (26.6) must lie within (-32768, 32768) to avoid overflow.
On success the caller owns the returned glyph and must release it with FT_Done_Glyph.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Glyph_Copy
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Error ) FT_Glyph_Copy( FT_Glyph   source, FT_Glyph  *target );
functions.description: Create a duplicate of a glyph image. The new FT_Glyph is independent from the source and must be released with FT_Done_Glyph.
requirements: source must be a valid FT_Glyph handle to copy.
target must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the copied FT_Glyph; it is set to NULL on error.
On success the caller owns the returned glyph and must release it with FT_Done_Glyph.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Glyph_Transform
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Error ) FT_Glyph_Transform( FT_Glyph          glyph, const FT_Matrix*  matrix, const FT_Vector*  delta );
functions.description: Apply a 2x2 affine transform and optional translation to a glyph image, if the glyph’s format is scalable. The same transform is applied to the glyph’s advance vector. Returns an error if the glyph format is not scalable.
requirements: glyph must be a valid FT_Glyph handle whose format is scalable (e.g., outline/SVG where supported).
matrix must point to a valid 2x2 FT_Matrix to apply.
delta must point to a valid FT_Vector; coordinates are in 1/64 pixels (26.6).
Check the returned FT_Error; non-zero indicates failure (e.g., glyph not scalable).

functions.name: FT_Glyph_Get_CBox
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( void ) FT_Glyph_Get_CBox( FT_Glyph  glyph, FT_UInt   bbox_mode, FT_BBox  *acbox );
functions.description: Compute the glyph’s control box (CBox), which encloses all outline points including Bézier control points. It is fast and may be slightly larger than the exact bounding box. The returned box interpretation depends on bbox_mode (unscaled, 26.6 unfitted, 26.6 grid-fitted, integer pixels, or grid-fitted pixels).
requirements: glyph must be a valid FT_Glyph handle.
acbox must be a non-NULL pointer to an FT_BBox to receive results.
bbox_mode must be one of FT_GLYPH_BBOX_UNSCALED, FT_GLYPH_BBOX_SUBPIXELS, FT_GLYPH_BBOX_GRIDFIT, FT_GLYPH_BBOX_TRUNCATE, or FT_GLYPH_BBOX_PIXELS.
If the glyph was loaded with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE and unscaled font units are desired, set bbox_mode to FT_GLYPH_BBOX_UNSCALED.
For ‘tricky’ fonts loaded with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE, CBox values may be meaningless unless the glyph is loaded at a large ppem first.

functions.name: FT_Glyph_To_Bitmap
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Error ) FT_Glyph_To_Bitmap( FT_Glyph*         the_glyph, FT_Render_Mode    render_mode, const FT_Vector*  origin, FT_Bool           destroy );
functions.description: Convert a scalable glyph to a bitmap glyph (FT_BitmapGlyph). Optionally translate by origin before rendering, choose a render mode, and optionally destroy the original glyph. On success, *the_glyph is replaced with a newly allocated bitmap glyph.
requirements: the_glyph must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid FT_Glyph handle; on success it is replaced by a new glyph.
render_mode selects how the glyph is rendered (e.g., FT_RENDER_MODE_NORMAL, FT_RENDER_MODE_MONO).
origin may be NULL (no translation) or point to a vector in 26.6 pixels to translate prior to rendering.
If destroy is true, the original glyph is destroyed on success; it is never destroyed on error.
This function does nothing if the glyph format is not scalable.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Done_Glyph
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( void ) FT_Done_Glyph( FT_Glyph  glyph );
functions.description: Destroy and free a glyph object previously created or returned by FreeType glyph functions. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: Call to release any FT_Glyph obtained from FT_New_Glyph, FT_Get_Glyph, FT_Glyph_Copy, or FT_Glyph_To_Bitmap.
glyph may be NULL (the function is a no-op in that case).

functions.name: FT_Matrix_Multiply
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( void ) FT_Matrix_Multiply( const FT_Matrix*  a, FT_Matrix*        b );
functions.description: Compute b = a * b for 2x2 matrices using fixed-point arithmetic. Operates in place on b. Intended for composing transforms.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid FT_Matrix.
b must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid FT_Matrix to be overwritten with the result.
Behavior is undefined if either matrix a or b is the zero matrix (all elements zero).
Wrap-around arithmetic is used; very large values can yield meaningless results.

functions.name: FT_Matrix_Invert
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Error ) FT_Matrix_Invert( FT_Matrix*  matrix );
functions.description: Invert a 2x2 matrix in place. Leaves the matrix unchanged and returns an error if it is not invertible.
requirements: matrix must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid FT_Matrix.
On failure (non-invertible), the matrix contents remain unchanged.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Outline_MoveTo_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Outline_MoveTo_Func)( const FT_Vector* to, void* user );
functions.description: Callback type invoked during outline decomposition to start a new contour (a “move to”). Returns 0 on success. The callee typically updates its current position to the point referenced by ‘to’.
requirements: to must point to a valid FT_Vector containing the target point.
user is an opaque caller-supplied pointer and may be NULL.
Return 0 to signal success; any non-zero value signals an error to the decomposer.

functions.name: FT_Outline_LineTo_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Outline_LineTo_Func)( const FT_Vector* to, void* user );
functions.description: Callback type invoked during outline decomposition to emit a straight line segment from the current point to ‘to’. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: to must point to a valid FT_Vector containing the target point.
user is an opaque caller-supplied pointer and may be NULL.
Return 0 to signal success; any non-zero value signals an error to the decomposer.

functions.name: FT_Outline_ConicTo_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Outline_ConicTo_Func)( const FT_Vector* control, const FT_Vector* to, void* user );
functions.description: Callback type invoked during outline decomposition to emit a second‑order (quadratic) Bézier curve from the current point to ‘to’ using ‘control’ as the single control point. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: control must point to a valid FT_Vector containing the quadratic control point.
to must point to a valid FT_Vector containing the curve end point.
user is an opaque caller-supplied pointer and may be NULL.
Return 0 to signal success; any non-zero value signals an error to the decomposer.

functions.name: FT_Outline_CubicTo_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Outline_CubicTo_Func)( const FT_Vector* control1, const FT_Vector* control2, const FT_Vector* to, void* user );
functions.description: Callback type invoked during outline decomposition to emit a third‑order (cubic) Bézier curve from the current point to ‘to’ using ‘control1’ and ‘control2’ as the two control points. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: control1 must point to a valid FT_Vector (first cubic control point).
control2 must point to a valid FT_Vector (second cubic control point).
to must point to a valid FT_Vector containing the curve end point.
user is an opaque caller-supplied pointer and may be NULL.
Return 0 to signal success; any non-zero value signals an error to the decomposer.

functions.name: FT_Raster_Span_Func
functions.signature: void (*FT_Raster_Span_Func)( int y, int count, const FT_Span* spans, void* user );
functions.description: Callback type used by the anti‑aliased raster to deliver spans (runs of pixels with the same coverage) for a given scanline y. The callee draws or composites the ‘count’ spans starting at spans[0].
requirements: y is the upward scanline coordinate supplied by the raster.
count is the number of spans to process and must be >= 0.
spans points to an array of ‘count’ FT_Span elements; each span’s length (len) and coverage (0..255) should be honored.
user is an opaque caller-supplied pointer and may be NULL.
This callback is used only for anti-aliased rendering and in direct rendering mode when FT_RASTER_FLAG_AA (and typically FT_RASTER_FLAG_DIRECT) are set.

functions.name: FT_Raster_BitTest_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Raster_BitTest_Func)( int y, int x, void* user );
functions.description: Deprecated, unimplemented callback type intended for monochrome bit testing. It is not used by current FreeType rasters.
requirements: This function is deprecated and marked unimplemented in the header; callers should not rely on it.
If implemented by a custom raster, ‘y’ and ‘x’ are pixel coordinates; ‘user’ is opaque and may be NULL. Return value semantics are unspecified by FreeType (unknown).

functions.name: FT_Raster_BitSet_Func
functions.signature: void (*FT_Raster_BitSet_Func)( int y, int x, void* user );
functions.description: Deprecated, unimplemented callback type intended for monochrome bit setting. It is not used by current FreeType rasters.
requirements: This function is deprecated and marked unimplemented in the header; callers should not rely on it.
If implemented by a custom raster, ‘y’ and ‘x’ are pixel coordinates; ‘user’ is opaque and may be NULL. Behavioral semantics are unspecified by FreeType (unknown).

functions.name: FT_Raster_New_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Raster_New_Func)( void* memory, FT_Raster* raster );
functions.description: Constructor function type for creating a raster object. On success returns 0 and stores a new raster handle in *raster. ‘memory’ is a typeless allocator handle (typically FT_Memory).
requirements: raster must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created FT_Raster handle.
On success the function returns 0; non-zero indicates an error.
memory is an opaque allocator handle and may be ignored by an implementation.

functions.name: FT_Raster_Done_Func
functions.signature: void (*FT_Raster_Done_Func)( FT_Raster raster );
functions.description: Destructor function type for destroying a raster object created by FT_Raster_New_Func.
requirements: raster must be a valid FT_Raster previously created by the corresponding raster_new function.
After this call, the raster handle must not be used again.

functions.name: FT_Raster_Reset_Func
functions.signature: void (*FT_Raster_Reset_Func)( FT_Raster raster, unsigned char* pool_base, unsigned long pool_size );
functions.description: Initialization/reset function type called after creating a raster object. Historic render-pool parameters are no longer used; FreeType never allocates this pool now.
requirements: raster must be a valid FT_Raster to reset/initialize.
pool_base must be set to NULL and pool_size must be set to 0 as the shared render pool is no longer used.

functions.name: FT_Raster_Set_Mode_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Raster_Set_Mode_Func)( FT_Raster raster, unsigned long mode, void* args );
functions.description: Generic facility to change raster modes or properties identified by a 4‑byte tag ‘mode’. Semantics of each mode and the data pointed to by ‘args’ are implementation-specific. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: raster must be a valid FT_Raster.
mode is a 4-byte tag selecting a mode/property; its accepted values are raster-implementation specific.
args must point to the value/data required by the selected mode; content and size are implementation-specific and may be NULL if the mode requires no data.
Return 0 on success; non-zero on error.

functions.name: FT_Raster_Render_Func
functions.signature: int (*FT_Raster_Render_Func)( FT_Raster raster, const FT_Raster_Params* params );
functions.description: Invokes the raster to convert a source glyph image into a target bitmap or to emit spans, according to params. Returns 0 on success. The source format must match the raster’s glyph_format.
requirements: raster must be a valid FT_Raster.
params must point to a valid FT_Raster_Params structure.
If FT_RASTER_FLAG_AA is not set in params->flags, a monochrome (1-bit) bitmap is generated; if set, anti-aliased rendering is performed.
If FT_RASTER_FLAG_DIRECT is set, the raster ignores params->target and calls params->gray_spans for span output; for clipping in this mode, also set FT_RASTER_FLAG_CLIP and provide params->clip_box.
Direct rendering is only possible with anti-aliased glyphs; rasters may fail with FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature if direct composition is not supported.
When not using direct mode, the target bitmap’s buffer must be zeroed before rendering and output is clipped to the target bitmap’s size.
The exact type of params->source depends on the raster’s supported glyph format (for the smooth/bilevel raster it is typically an FT_Outline).
Return 0 on success; non-zero on error.

functions.name: FT_Get_Advance
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Advance(FT_Face face, FT_UInt gindex, FT_Int32 load_flags, FT_Fixed* padvance);
functions.description: Retrieve the advance value for a single glyph in an FT_Face without loading/processing the glyph outline when possible. Returns a FreeType error code; on success writes the advance to padvance. If FT_LOAD_VERTICAL_LAYOUT is set in load_flags, returns the vertical advance; otherwise the horizontal advance. If scaling is performed according to load_flags, the value is in 16.16 fixed-point; otherwise it is in font units. Not affected by any transform set via FT_Set_Transform. If FT_ADVANCE_FLAG_FAST_ONLY is OR-ed into load_flags and a fast path is not available, the function may fail.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face handle.
gindex must be a valid glyph index in the given face (i.e., refer to an existing glyph).
padvance must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for one FT_Fixed result.
Caller must inspect the returned FT_Error; a non-zero value indicates failure and padvance must not be used.
If FT_LOAD_VERTICAL_LAYOUT is set in load_flags, caller should expect a vertical advance; otherwise a horizontal advance.
If scaling is requested via load_flags, the returned advance is in 16.16 fixed-point; otherwise it is in font units.
If FT_ADVANCE_FLAG_FAST_ONLY is set in load_flags, the call may fail when a quick advance computation is not available; caller must handle this error.
Returned advances are not transformed by FT_Set_Transform; apply any desired transform manually if needed.

functions.name: FT_Get_Advances
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Advances(FT_Face face, FT_UInt start, FT_UInt count, FT_Int32 load_flags, FT_Fixed* padvances);
functions.description: Retrieve advance values for a range of glyphs in an FT_Face without loading/processing outlines when possible. Returns a FreeType error code; on success writes count advances to padvances starting at glyph index start. If FT_LOAD_VERTICAL_LAYOUT is set in load_flags, returns vertical advances; otherwise horizontal. If scaling is performed according to load_flags, values are in 16.16 fixed-point; otherwise in font units. Not affected by FT_Set_Transform. If FT_ADVANCE_FLAG_FAST_ONLY is set and a fast path is not available, the function may fail.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face handle.
The glyph index range [start, start + count) must refer to valid glyph indices in the face.
count specifies how many advances to retrieve; when count > 0, padvances must be non-null and point to writable storage for at least count FT_Fixed elements.
Caller must inspect the returned FT_Error; a non-zero value indicates failure and padvances content is unspecified.
If FT_LOAD_VERTICAL_LAYOUT is set in load_flags, caller should expect vertical advances; otherwise horizontal advances.
If scaling is requested via load_flags, the returned advances are in 16.16 fixed-point; otherwise they are in font units.
If FT_ADVANCE_FLAG_FAST_ONLY is set in load_flags, the call may fail when a quick advance computation is not available; caller must handle this error.
Returned advances are not transformed by FT_Set_Transform; apply any desired transform manually if needed.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Get_BBox
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Get_BBox( FT_Outline* outline, FT_BBox* abbox );
functions.description: Computes the exact bounding box of a FreeType outline by examining curve extrema. Slower than computing the control box, but optimized to return quickly if both boxes coincide. Typical use: after loading a glyph outline, call this to obtain its precise bounds. Note: for tricky fonts loaded with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE, the resulting bounding box is meaningless; load at a large ppem to let hinting position subglyphs, then (if needed) convert the resulting box back to font units.
requirements: outline must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized FT_Outline whose points describe the outline to be measured.
abbox must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for the resulting FT_BBox.
Callers must check the returned FT_Error; 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure.

If the font is tricky and the glyph was loaded with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE, the returned bounding box is meaningless; to obtain reasonable values, load the glyph at a large ppem first and compute the bbox there, converting back to font units if required.

functions.name: FT_Get_BDF_Charset_ID
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_BDF_Charset_ID( FT_Face face, const char** acharset_encoding, const char** acharset_registry )
functions.description: Retrieve the BDF charset encoding and registry strings from a face. Intended for BDF faces and SFNT bitmap fonts that contain a 'BDF~' table (e.g., X11 .otb). On success, returns encoding and registry as C strings owned by the face; the caller must not free them. Returns a FreeType error code (0 means success).
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face referring to either a BDF face or an SFNT face that contains a 'BDF~' table.
For SFNT fonts with a 'BDF~' table, a bitmap strike size must be selected before calling this function.
acharset_encoding must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the address of a NUL-terminated C string; the returned string is owned by the face and must not be freed by the caller.
acharset_registry must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the address of a NUL-terminated C string; the returned string is owned by the face and must not be freed by the caller.
Callers must check the returned FT_Error; only use output values if the return value is 0 (success).

functions.name: FT_Get_BDF_Property
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_BDF_Property( FT_Face face, const char* prop_name, BDF_PropertyRec* aproperty )
functions.description: Retrieve a named BDF/PCF property from a font. Works with BDF and PCF faces, and with SFNT bitmap fonts that carry a 'BDF~' table. On success, fills aproperty with the property's type and value (atom/integer/cardinal). Returns a FreeType error code (0 means success). On error, aproperty->type is set to BDF_PROPERTY_TYPE_NONE.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face referring to a BDF or PCF face; alternatively, an SFNT face that contains a 'BDF~' table.
For SFNT fonts with a 'BDF~' table, a bitmap strike size must be selected before calling this function.
prop_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string naming the property to retrieve.
aproperty must point to writable storage; the function writes the result into *aproperty.
If the property is not in the font, the function returns an error and sets aproperty->type to BDF_PROPERTY_TYPE_NONE; callers must check the returned FT_Error before using aproperty.
Integer properties in PCF are stored as signed; BDF_PROPERTY_TYPE_CARDINAL may be returned only for BDF fonts (not PCF).

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_Init
functions.signature: void FT_Bitmap_Init( FT_Bitmap *abitmap );
functions.description: Initialize an FT_Bitmap structure. Intended to prepare a bitmap object for later use by other FT_Bitmap utility functions. Details of initial field values are not explicitly documented here; typical usage is to call this on a fresh FT_Bitmap and then set desired fields (for example, pitch sign to control flow) before further operations. Deprecated alias: FT_Bitmap_New.
requirements: abitmap must be a valid, writable pointer to an FT_Bitmap structure.

If you need a specific bitmap flow (top-down or bottom-up), set the FT_Bitmap::pitch sign after FT_Bitmap_Init and before calling other bitmap functions (as noted in the header’s section description).

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_New
functions.signature: void FT_Bitmap_New( FT_Bitmap *abitmap );
functions.description: Deprecated alias for FT_Bitmap_Init. Initializes an FT_Bitmap structure for subsequent use by FreeType bitmap utilities. Details of initial field values are not explicitly documented here.
requirements: abitmap must be a valid, writable pointer to an FT_Bitmap structure.
If you need a specific bitmap flow (top-down or bottom-up), set the FT_Bitmap::pitch sign after initialization and before calling other bitmap functions.

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_Copy
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Bitmap_Copy( FT_Library library, const FT_Bitmap *source, FT_Bitmap *target );
functions.description: Copy the contents of one bitmap to another, allocating or resizing the target buffer as needed using the library’s memory routines. Returns 0 on success, an FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle (used for memory handling).
source must point to a valid FT_Bitmap to read from.
target must point to a valid FT_Bitmap to receive the copy (its buffer will be (re)allocated as needed).
source->buffer and target->buffer must neither be equal nor overlap.

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_Embolden
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Bitmap_Embolden( FT_Library library, FT_Bitmap* bitmap, FT_Pos xStrength, FT_Pos yStrength );
functions.description: Embolden (thicken) a bitmap in-place by approximately xStrength pixels horizontally and yStrength pixels vertically (strengths in 26.6 pixel units). The left and bottom edges are preserved. May convert GRAY2/GRAY bitmaps to 8bpp GRAY. Returns 0 on success, an FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
bitmap must point to the bitmap to be modified; it must be writable and properly initialized.
xStrength and yStrength are specified in 26.6 pixel format.
If bitmap->pixel_mode is FT_PIXEL_MODE_MONO, xStrength must be <= 8 (current implementation restriction).
If emboldening a bitmap from an FT_GlyphSlot, call FT_GlyphSlot_Own_Bitmap(slot) before emboldening to ensure the slot owns its bitmap buffer.

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_Convert
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Bitmap_Convert( FT_Library library, const FT_Bitmap *source, FT_Bitmap *target, FT_Int alignment );
functions.description: Convert a bitmap with depth 1, 2, 4, 8, or 32 bpp to an 8 bpp bitmap. The resulting target pitch will be a multiple of alignment. The target buffer is allocated or reallocated as needed using the library’s memory routines. Returns 0 on success, an FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle (used for memory handling).
source must be a valid FT_Bitmap with a depth of 1, 2, 4, 8, or 32 bpp.
target must point to a valid FT_Bitmap to receive the converted data; its buffer will be allocated or reallocated as needed.
alignment should be chosen such that the target pitch can be a multiple of it (common values are 1, 2, or 4).
It is permitted to call FT_Bitmap_Convert repeatedly on the same target without FT_Bitmap_Done in between (the memory is reallocated).
source->buffer and target->buffer must neither be equal nor overlap.

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_Blend
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Bitmap_Blend( FT_Library library, const FT_Bitmap* source, const FT_Vector source_offset, FT_Bitmap* target, FT_Vector* atarget_offset, FT_Color color );
functions.description: Blend a source bitmap onto a target bitmap using the given color. The target is allocated or reallocated as needed and becomes BGRA with pitch set to 4 * width on (re)allocation. Offsets are in 26.6 pixel format; the function forces them to integer values by zeroing the lowest six bits. No clipping is performed. Returns 0 on success, an FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
source must be a valid FT_Bitmap; it may have any FT_Pixel_Mode.
source_offset should represent an integer offset in 26.6 pixel format; the function will zero the lowest six bits.
target must either be an empty, initialized FT_Bitmap (initialized via FT_Bitmap_Init) or already be of pixel mode FT_PIXEL_MODE_BGRA.
atarget_offset must be a valid, writable pointer; it provides the input target offset (26.6 format, integer-constrained) and is updated according to any allocation/reallocation.
No clipping is performed; caller should ensure the intended compositing area is acceptable.
On any (re)allocation, target->pitch is set to 4 * width.
source and target must have the same bitmap flow (same sign of FT_Bitmap::pitch).
source->buffer and target->buffer must neither be equal nor overlap.

functions.name: FT_GlyphSlot_Own_Bitmap
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_GlyphSlot_Own_Bitmap( FT_GlyphSlot slot );
functions.description: Ensure that an FT_GlyphSlot owns its bitmap buffer (i.e., the bitmap is unique to the slot and can be modified safely). Typically used before in-place bitmap modifications like FT_Bitmap_Embolden. Returns 0 on success, an FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: slot must be a valid FT_GlyphSlot handle.
Call this before modifying slot->bitmap (e.g., before FT_Bitmap_Embolden) to ensure the bitmap is owned by the slot.

functions.name: FT_Bitmap_Done
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Bitmap_Done( FT_Library library, FT_Bitmap *bitmap );
functions.description: Destroy a bitmap object that was initialized with FT_Bitmap_Init, releasing any associated buffer using the library’s memory routines. Returns 0 on success, an FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle (used for memory handling).
bitmap must point to a bitmap previously initialized with FT_Bitmap_Init (and potentially modified by other FT bitmap utilities).

functions.name: FT_Stream_OpenBzip2
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stream_OpenBzip2( FT_Stream stream, FT_Stream source );
functions.description: Opens a new FreeType stream that transparently reads from a bzip2-compressed source stream. Typically used to access compressed font files (e.g., *.pcf.bz2) so they can be consumed by FreeType like regular streams. The function initializes the target stream (stream) to wrap the already-open source stream (source). Note: closing the new stream does not close the source stream; the caller retains ownership and must manage both lifetimes. May return FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature if FreeType was built without bzip2 support.
requirements: source must be opened before calling this function (explicit in documentation).
stream is the target stream object provided by the caller and will be initialized by this function; caller retains ownership (explicit in documentation).
Calling FT_Stream_Close on stream will not close source; caller must close source separately (explicit in documentation).
None of the stream objects are released to the heap by this function; caller must manage memory/lifetimes (explicit in documentation).
On success returns 0; on failure returns a non-zero FreeType error code. Callers must check the return value (explicit in documentation).
Function may fail with FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature if FreeType was not compiled with bzip2 support (explicit in documentation).
Arguments must be valid FT_Stream handles (pointers) and non-NULL (inferred from types and typical FreeType conventions).
Intended for use with bzip2-compressed data; using a non-bzip2 source will result in an error during open or subsequent use (inferred from purpose).

functions.name: FTC_Manager_New
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_Manager_New(FT_Library library, FT_UInt max_faces, FT_UInt max_sizes, FT_ULong max_bytes, FTC_Face_Requester requester, FT_Pointer req_data, FTC_Manager *amanager);
functions.description: Create a new FreeType cache manager that controls a bounded number of FT_Face/FT_Size objects and caches data nodes. Usage: call once to obtain a FTC_Manager handle, then use it with lookup and cache APIs. Pass a requester to resolve FTC_FaceID to FT_Face; req_data is forwarded to that requester. Returns 0 on success and writes the manager handle to amanager.
requirements: library must be a valid, initialized FT_Library.
requester must be a valid callback capable of creating an FT_Face from a given FTC_FaceID and must not create FT_Size objects or set transformations on the returned face.
amanager must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the created manager handle.
max_faces, max_sizes, max_bytes may be 0 to request library defaults.
On error (non-zero return), amanager is 0 (NULL).

functions.name: FTC_Manager_Reset
functions.signature: void FTC_Manager_Reset(FTC_Manager manager);
functions.description: Empty the given cache manager, discarding all currently cached FT_Face and FT_Size objects and cache nodes, without destroying the manager itself.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager handle obtained from FTC_Manager_New.

functions.name: FTC_Manager_Done
functions.signature: void FTC_Manager_Done(FTC_Manager manager);
functions.description: Destroy the given cache manager after emptying it. All caches created under this manager are destroyed with it.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager handle created by FTC_Manager_New.
After this call, the manager handle must not be used again.

functions.name: FTC_Manager_LookupFace
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_Manager_LookupFace(FTC_Manager manager, FTC_FaceID face_id, FT_Face *aface);
functions.description: Retrieve (and possibly create) the FT_Face corresponding to face_id through the cache manager. The returned FT_Face is owned by the manager; do not free or transform it. Returns 0 on success and writes the face to aface.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager.
face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
aface must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the FT_Face.
Callers must not call FT_Done_Face, create FT_Size, or call FT_Set_Transform on the returned FT_Face.
On out-of-memory, the cache may flush incrementally; if FT_Err_Out_Of_Memory is returned, the cache has already been completely flushed.

functions.name: FTC_Manager_LookupSize
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_Manager_LookupSize(FTC_Manager manager, FTC_Scaler scaler, FT_Size *asize);
functions.description: Retrieve (and possibly create) the FT_Size corresponding to the scaler description through the cache manager. The returned FT_Size (and its parent FT_Face via size->face) are owned by the manager. Returns 0 on success and writes the size to asize.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager.
scaler must point to a valid FTC_ScalerRec describing face_id and size; when pixel==0, x_res and y_res are used; when pixel==1, width/height are pixel sizes.
scaler->face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
asize must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the FT_Size.
Callers must not free or modify the returned FT_Size or its FT_Face; they are owned by the manager.
On out-of-memory, the cache may flush incrementally; FT_Err_Out_Of_Memory means complete flush still insufficient.

functions.name: FTC_Node_Unref
functions.signature: void FTC_Node_Unref(FTC_Node node, FTC_Manager manager);
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of a cache node previously acquired from a cache lookup. When the count reaches 0, the node becomes eligible for cache flushes (not immediately destroyed).
requirements: node must be a cache node handle previously obtained from a cache lookup that returned a node and increased its refcount.
manager must be the cache manager that owns the node.
Each successful acquisition (via anode out-parameter from a lookup) should be paired with a corresponding FTC_Node_Unref call.

functions.name: FTC_Manager_RemoveFaceID
functions.signature: void FTC_Manager_RemoveFaceID(FTC_Manager manager, FTC_FaceID face_id);
functions.description: Notify the cache manager that a particular FTC_FaceID has become invalid (e.g., content changed, deallocated, or uninstalled). The cache flushes all nodes for that face_id except those still referenced; such remaining nodes are marked to never match future lookups and are destroyed once released.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager.
face_id must be the FTC_FaceID to invalidate; per documentation, face IDs must be persistent during normal operation and never be NULL.
Should be called as soon as possible after a face ID becomes invalid to avoid incorrect behaviour or crashes.

functions.name: FTC_CMapCache_New
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_CMapCache_New(FTC_Manager manager, FTC_CMapCache *acache);
functions.description: Create a new charmap cache used to accelerate character code to glyph index mapping. The cache is destroyed with its parent manager. Returns 0 on success and writes the cache handle to acache.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager.
acache must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the cache handle.

functions.name: FTC_CMapCache_Lookup
functions.signature: FT_UInt FTC_CMapCache_Lookup(FTC_CMapCache cache, FTC_FaceID face_id, FT_Int cmap_index, FT_UInt32 char_code);
functions.description: Translate a character code to a glyph index using the charmap cache. If cmap_index is negative, the FT_Face's default charmap is used. Returns 0 if there is no glyph.
requirements: cache must be a valid FTC_CMapCache.
face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
cmap_index < 0 means use the face's default charmap; otherwise, it should be a valid charmap index for the face.
char_code must be a valid code point for the selected charmap (no range is enforced by the API; unmapped codes yield 0).

functions.name: FTC_ImageCache_New
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_ImageCache_New(FTC_Manager manager, FTC_ImageCache *acache);
functions.description: Create a new glyph image cache for storing many glyph images under a memory threshold. The cache is destroyed with the manager. Returns 0 on success and writes the cache handle to acache.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager.
acache must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the image cache handle.

functions.name: FTC_ImageCache_Lookup
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_ImageCache_Lookup(FTC_ImageCache cache, FTC_ImageType type, FT_UInt gindex, FT_Glyph *aglyph, FTC_Node *anode);
functions.description: Retrieve a glyph image from the image cache for the given face/size/type and glyph index. On success, returns 0 and writes an FT_Glyph owned by the cache to aglyph. If anode is non-NULL, it receives the cache node with its refcount incremented; the caller must later unref it.
requirements: cache must be a valid FTC_ImageCache.
type must point to a valid FTC_ImageTypeRec describing face_id, width, height, and load flags.
type->face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
aglyph must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the FT_Glyph; the returned glyph is owned by the cache and must not be transformed or destroyed by the caller.
If anode is non-NULL, the caller must eventually call FTC_Node_Unref(*anode, manager) to release the reference.
If anode is NULL, the node is not pinned and the glyph may be flushed on subsequent cache operations.
To modify a glyph, make a private copy with FT_Glyph_Copy.

functions.name: FTC_ImageCache_LookupScaler
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_ImageCache_LookupScaler(FTC_ImageCache cache, FTC_Scaler scaler, FT_ULong load_flags, FT_UInt gindex, FT_Glyph *aglyph, FTC_Node *anode);
functions.description: Retrieve a glyph image from the image cache using an FTC_ScalerRec to specify face and size plus explicit load flags. Semantics and ownership are like FTC_ImageCache_Lookup. Returns 0 on success and writes the FT_Glyph to aglyph; optionally returns/pins the cache node in anode.
requirements: cache must be a valid FTC_ImageCache.
scaler must point to a valid FTC_ScalerRec; scaler->face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
aglyph must be a non-NULL, writable pointer; returned glyph is owned by the cache and must not be transformed or freed by the caller.
If anode is non-NULL, the caller must eventually call FTC_Node_Unref to release the reference; if NULL, the glyph/node may be flushed later.
Calls to FT_Set_Char_Size and related APIs do not affect cached glyphs; use the cache API (i.e., this function) to select sizes.

functions.name: FTC_SBitCache_New
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_SBitCache_New(FTC_Manager manager, FTC_SBitCache *acache);
functions.description: Create a new small-bitmap (sbit) cache for storing small glyph bitmaps/pixmaps efficiently. The cache is destroyed with the manager. Returns 0 on success and writes the cache handle to acache.
requirements: manager must be a valid FTC_Manager.
acache must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the sbit cache handle.

functions.name: FTC_SBitCache_Lookup
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_SBitCache_Lookup(FTC_SBitCache cache, FTC_ImageType type, FT_UInt gindex, FTC_SBit *sbit, FTC_Node *anode);
functions.description: Look up a small glyph bitmap in the sbit cache and optionally lock its node. On success, returns 0 and writes an FTC_SBit descriptor; the descriptor and its buffer are owned by the cache and may disappear on subsequent operations unless pinned via anode. The descriptor’s buffer is set to 0 to indicate a missing glyph bitmap.
requirements: cache must be a valid FTC_SBitCache.
type must point to a valid FTC_ImageTypeRec describing the requested face/size and load flags.
type->face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
sbit must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the descriptor.
If anode is non-NULL, the function increments the node’s reference count; the caller must later call FTC_Node_Unref to release it. If anode is NULL, the node may be flushed subsequently.
The sbit descriptor and its buffer must not be freed or retained beyond their validity; they are cache-owned and not persistent unless pinned.

functions.name: FTC_SBitCache_LookupScaler
functions.signature: FT_Error FTC_SBitCache_LookupScaler(FTC_SBitCache cache, FTC_Scaler scaler, FT_ULong load_flags, FT_UInt gindex, FTC_SBit *sbit, FTC_Node *anode);
functions.description: Variant of FTC_SBitCache_Lookup that uses an FTC_ScalerRec and explicit load flags to specify face and size. Returns 0 on success and writes an FTC_SBit descriptor owned by the cache; optionally returns the cache node with increased refcount in anode.
requirements: cache must be a valid FTC_SBitCache.
scaler must point to a valid FTC_ScalerRec; scaler->face_id must be a valid, persistent, non-NULL FTC_FaceID.
sbit must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to receive the descriptor; descriptor and buffer are owned by the cache and must not be freed by the caller.
If anode is non-NULL, the caller must eventually call FTC_Node_Unref to release the node; if NULL, the node/bitmap may be flushed later.

functions.name: FT_Get_CID_Registry_Ordering_Supplement
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_CID_Registry_Ordering_Supplement(FT_Face face, const char** registry, const char** ordering, FT_Int* supplement);
functions.description: Returns the Registry/Ordering/Supplement (R/O/S) triple from a CID‑keyed font. The registry and ordering are returned as C strings that are owned by the FT_Face and remain valid as long as the face is alive. Use this to identify the character collection associated with a CID font. Only works with CID faces; non‑CID faces return an error. Returns 0 on success, otherwise a FreeType error code.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face loaded by FreeType.
The function only succeeds for CID faces; it returns an error otherwise.
registry must point to writable storage for a const char* output (the returned string is owned by the face).
ordering must point to writable storage for a const char* output (the returned string is owned by the face).
supplement must point to writable storage for an FT_Int output.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error (0 means success).
The lifetime of the returned strings is tied to the FT_Face; do not free them and do not use them after the face is destroyed.

functions.name: FT_Get_CID_Is_Internally_CID_Keyed
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_CID_Is_Internally_CID_Keyed(FT_Face face, FT_Bool* is_cid);
functions.description: Determines whether the face is internally CID‑keyed. Unlike the FT_IS_CID_KEYED macro, this also works for CID‑keyed fonts wrapped in SFNT/OpenType. Only works with CID faces and OpenType fonts; returns an error otherwise. Returns 0 on success, otherwise a FreeType error code.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face loaded by FreeType.
The function only succeeds for CID faces and OpenType fonts; it returns an error otherwise.
is_cid must point to writable storage for an FT_Bool output.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error (0 means success).

functions.name: FT_Get_CID_From_Glyph_Index
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_CID_From_Glyph_Index(FT_Face face, FT_UInt glyph_index, FT_UInt* cid);
functions.description: Maps a glyph index in the face to its CID value and returns it via cid. Use to obtain the CID corresponding to a glyph slot index. Only works with CID faces and OpenType fonts; returns an error otherwise. Returns 0 on success, otherwise a FreeType error code.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face loaded by FreeType.
glyph_index should be a valid glyph index for the given face (within the face’s glyph count).
The function only succeeds for CID faces and OpenType fonts; it returns an error otherwise.
cid must point to writable storage for an FT_UInt output.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error (0 means success).

functions.name: FT_Palette_Data_Get
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Palette_Data_Get(FT_Face face, FT_Palette_Data* apalette);
functions.description: Retrieve the CPAL palette metadata for a face into an FT_Palette_Data structure. Arrays exposed via the returned structure are read-only and describe palette count, flags, and entry name IDs. Use FT_Get_Sfnt_Name to resolve name IDs and FT_Palette_Select to get actual colors.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
apalette must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the palette metadata.
All arrays in the returned FT_Palette_Data are read-only; do not modify or free them.
Returns 0 on success; on failure a non-zero FT_Error is returned.
This function always returns an error if TT_CONFIG_OPTION_COLOR_LAYERS is not defined in ftoption.h.

functions.name: FT_Palette_Select
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Palette_Select(FT_Face face, FT_UShort palette_index, FT_Color** apalette);
functions.description: Activate a CPAL palette for color-glyph rendering and optionally retrieve a read-write array of its FT_Color entries. The returned array is owned by FreeType; you may modify entries, but subsequent calls with the same arguments reset them to the original CPAL values.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
palette_index should refer to an existing palette for the face (as reported by FT_Palette_Data_Get).
apalette may be NULL to only activate the palette without retrieving the array.
If the font has no color palettes, the returned array is NULL.
The color array is owned/managed by FreeType; do not free it. Modifications are not persistent across subsequent calls.
Returns 0 on success; on failure a non-zero FT_Error is returned.
This function always returns an error if TT_CONFIG_OPTION_COLOR_LAYERS is not defined in ftoption.h.

functions.name: FT_Palette_Set_Foreground_Color
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Palette_Set_Foreground_Color(FT_Face face, FT_Color foreground_color);
functions.description: Set the special CPAL index 0xFFFF “text foreground color” used by COLR glyphs. If not called, FreeType uses a default (white opaque if the current palette is flagged for dark backgrounds; black opaque otherwise).
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
foreground_color must be a valid FT_Color in sRGB, non–premultiplied alpha.
Returns 0 on success; on failure a non-zero FT_Error is returned.
This function always returns an error if TT_CONFIG_OPTION_COLOR_LAYERS is not defined in ftoption.h.

functions.name: FT_Get_Color_Glyph_Layer
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Get_Color_Glyph_Layer(FT_Face face, FT_UInt base_glyph, FT_UInt* aglyph_index, FT_UInt* acolor_index, FT_LayerIterator* iterator);
functions.description: Iterate over COLR v0 glyph layers for base_glyph. On each call, returns one layer’s glyph index and its CPAL color index in z-order (bottom to top). Initialize iterator->p = NULL before the first call and repeat calls until 0 is returned.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
base_glyph must be a valid glyph index for the face.
iterator must be non-NULL; set iterator->p = NULL before the first call; reuse the same iterator for subsequent calls.
aglyph_index must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the layer glyph index.
acolor_index must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the CPAL color index; value 0xFFFF indicates use of the text foreground color.
Returns 1 while layers are available; returns 0 when no (more) layers exist or on error.

functions.name: FT_Get_Color_Glyph_Paint
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Get_Color_Glyph_Paint(FT_Face face, FT_UInt base_glyph, FT_Color_Root_Transform root_transform, FT_OpaquePaint* paint);
functions.description: Retrieve the root COLR v1 paint for the specified glyph. Optionally prepend a root transform (per current size and FT_Set_Transform) as an initial FT_PaintTransform node, controlled by root_transform. Use the returned FT_OpaquePaint with FT_Get_Paint to access concrete paint details.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face with a COLR v1 table for base_glyph to succeed.
base_glyph must be a valid glyph index for the face.
paint must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the opaque paint reference; do not preset its fields (it is output).
root_transform controls whether an initial root transform is returned (FT_COLOR_INCLUDE_ROOT_TRANSFORM) or omitted (FT_COLOR_NO_ROOT_TRANSFORM).
Returns 1 on success; returns 0 if no color glyph is found, the root paint cannot be retrieved, or on error.

functions.name: FT_Get_Color_Glyph_ClipBox
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Get_Color_Glyph_ClipBox(FT_Face face, FT_UInt base_glyph, FT_ClipBox* clip_box);
functions.description: Retrieve the COLR v1 ClipBox for base_glyph, if present. The returned box is computed in the current face scale and transform and reported as four 26.6 fixed-point FT_Vector corners.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
base_glyph must be a valid glyph index for the face.
clip_box must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the clip box if found.
Returns 1 if a clip box is found; returns 0 if none is present or on error.
To get the clip box in font units, set the scale to units-per-em and clear any transforms set with FT_Set_Transform before calling.

functions.name: FT_Get_Paint_Layers
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Get_Paint_Layers(FT_Face face, FT_LayerIterator* iterator, FT_OpaquePaint* paint);
functions.description: Iterate the layers of a PaintColrLayers node. Given the FT_LayerIterator from an FT_PaintColrLayers (obtained via FT_Get_Paint), returns one FT_OpaquePaint reference per call for each layer, advancing the iterator.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
iterator must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from an FT_PaintColrLayers structure; its internal state is advanced per call.
paint must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the next layer’s FT_OpaquePaint.
Returns 1 on success; returns 0 when no further layer can be retrieved or on error.

functions.name: FT_Get_Colorline_Stops
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Get_Colorline_Stops(FT_Face face, FT_ColorStop* color_stop, FT_ColorStopIterator* iterator);
functions.description: Iterate over the stops in a ColorLine (from linear or radial gradient paints). Supply the FT_ColorStopIterator obtained via FT_Get_Paint on an FT_ColorLine; each call returns one FT_ColorStop until none remain.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.
iterator must be a non-NULL FT_ColorStopIterator configured on an FT_ColorLine returned from FT_Get_Paint; do not manually modify its fields.
color_stop must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the stop (offset and color).
Returns 1 while more stops exist; returns 0 when iteration is complete or on error.

functions.name: FT_Get_Paint
functions.signature: FT_Bool FT_Get_Paint(FT_Face face, FT_OpaquePaint opaque_paint, FT_COLR_Paint* paint);
functions.description: Resolve an FT_OpaquePaint reference to its concrete FT_COLR_Paint details (format and data for Paint* tables). Use this to traverse the COLR v1 paint DAG by resolving nested FT_OpaquePaint references.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face.

opaque_paint must be a valid opaque reference. If the caller constructs it, set opaque_paint.p = NULL before passing; when obtained from FreeType (e.g., FT_Get_Color_Glyph_Paint or FT_Get_Paint_Layers), pass it as provided.
paint must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resolved FT_COLR_Paint.
Returns 1 on success; returns 0 if no details can be found for the paint or on error.

functions.name: FT_Error_String
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( const char* ) FT_Error_String( FT_Error error_code );
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for a given FreeType error code. Typical usage is to pass an FT_Error value returned by other FreeType APIs and receive a const C string; if the library was not built with error string support, the function returns NULL. Module-specific prefixes in error codes are ignored for the purpose of selecting the message, so the same base error maps to the same string regardless of module.
requirements: error_code must be a valid FreeType error code value (e.g., values defined via FT_Err_*).
The library must be built with FT_CONFIG_OPTION_ERROR_STRINGS or FT_DEBUG_LEVEL_ERROR to obtain meaningful non-NULL descriptions; otherwise the function may return NULL.
Callers must handle a possible NULL return value (check before dereferencing or printing).
The returned C string is const; callers must not modify it.

functions.name: FT_Get_Font_Format
functions.signature: const char* FT_Get_Font_Format(FT_Face face);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string that describes the font format of the given FreeType face (e.g., "TrueType", "Type 1", "BDF", "PCF", "Type 42", "CID Type 1", "CFF", "PFR", or "Windows FNT"). Intended for situations (such as some PDF/X11 workflows) where distinguishing the underlying font format matters despite FreeType’s uniform API. On failure, returns NULL.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face created by FreeType (e.g., via FT_New_Face)
The FreeType library must be initialized before creating the FT_Face (e.g., via FT_Init_FreeType)
face should not be NULL; if it is invalid or on other errors, the function may return NULL
Callers must check the return value for NULL before use
The returned string must not be modified or freed by the caller (const char*)

functions.name: FT_Get_X11_Font_Format
functions.signature: const char* FT_Get_X11_Font_Format(FT_Face face);
functions.description: Deprecated alias of FT_Get_Font_Format. Returns a string describing the font format of the given FT_Face, suitable for use as an X11 FONT_PROPERTY. On failure, returns NULL. Prefer using FT_Get_Font_Format instead.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face created by FreeType (e.g., via FT_New_Face)
The FreeType library must be initialized before creating the FT_Face (e.g., via FT_Init_FreeType)
face should not be NULL; if it is invalid or on other errors, the function may return NULL
Callers must check the return value for NULL before use
The returned string must not be modified or freed by the caller (const char*)
Usage is deprecated; prefer FT_Get_Font_Format

functions.name: FT_Get_Gasp
functions.signature: FT_EXPORT( FT_Int ) FT_Get_Gasp( FT_Face face, FT_UInt ppem );
functions.description: Returns the rasterizer behavior flags from a TrueType/OpenType font’s 'gasp' table for the specified vertical pixel size (ppem). Use this to determine whether to apply grid-fitting (hinting), grayscale smoothing, or ClearType-related behaviors at a given size. Returns FT_GASP_NO_TABLE if the face has no 'gasp' table. When working with OpenType variation fonts, call this after setting the variation instance (e.g., via FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates) since results can change with the instance.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle loaded by FreeType.
The face should correspond to a TrueType or OpenType font for meaningful 'gasp' data; otherwise the function may return FT_GASP_NO_TABLE.
ppem specifies the vertical character pixel size to query (in pixels).
If using OpenType variation (MM) functionality, set the desired variation instance before calling this function (e.g., via FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates).

Callers must inspect the return value: interpret the bit flags (FT_GASP_DO_GRIDFIT, FT_GASP_DO_GRAY, FT_GASP_SYMMETRIC_GRIDFIT, FT_GASP_SYMMETRIC_SMOOTHING) and handle the special value FT_GASP_NO_TABLE.

functions.name: FT_TrueTypeGX_Validate
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_TrueTypeGX_Validate( FT_Face face, FT_UInt validation_flags, FT_Bytes tables[FT_VALIDATE_GX_LENGTH], FT_UInt table_length );
functions.description: Validate selected TrueTypeGX/AAT tables in the given face, ensuring all offsets and indices are sane so higher-level layout code can use the tables without further checks. Usage: choose table types via FT_VALIDATE_GXXXX flags, provide an output array to receive per-table buffers, and typically pass FT_VALIDATE_GX_LENGTH as table_length. On success (return 0), non-NULL entries in tables contain validated table data that must later be freed with FT_TrueTypeGX_Free.
