If a table is absent, not requested, or unsupported by the validator, the corresponding entry is set to NULL. Only works with TrueTypeGX fonts; otherwise returns an error.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle; the function only works on TrueTypeGX/AAT fonts (non-GX faces cause an error).
validation_flags must be a bit-field composed of FT_VALIDATE_GXXXX constants (e.g., FT_VALIDATE_feat, FT_VALIDATE_morx, or FT_VALIDATE_GX).
tables must point to an array allocated by the caller with capacity for at least table_length elements of type FT_Bytes.
table_length should normally be FT_VALIDATE_GX_LENGTH and must not exceed the actual tables array capacity provided by the caller.
On success, each non-NULL tables[i] points to a buffer owned by FreeType and must be released by calling FT_TrueTypeGX_Free with the same face.
Callers must check the returned FT_Error; 0 indicates success.

functions.name: FT_TrueTypeGX_Free
functions.signature: void FT_TrueTypeGX_Free( FT_Face face, FT_Bytes table );
functions.description: Release a buffer previously returned by FT_TrueTypeGX_Validate (i.e., an entry from its tables[] array). Intended solely for deallocating those validator-allocated buffers.
requirements: Use only to free buffers that were produced by FT_TrueTypeGX_Validate.
face should be the same FT_Face (from the same FT_Library instance) that was used when obtaining the buffer (inferred from FreeType API patterns and the function signature).
Do not attempt to free such buffers with standard memory deallocation functions; use this API instead.

functions.name: FT_ClassicKern_Validate
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_ClassicKern_Validate( FT_Face face, FT_UInt validation_flags, FT_Bytes *ckern_table );
functions.description: Validate a classic (16-bit format) 'kern' table in the given face, ensuring offsets and indices are valid. Unlike the GX validator (which handles both classic and 32-bit formats), this function validates only the classic 16-bit dialect. The dialect to accept is selected with FT_VALIDATE_CKERNXXX flags; if the actual table does not match the selected dialect(s), validation fails. On success, returns 0 and sets *ckern_table to a buffer that must be freed with FT_ClassicKern_Free. If the face lacks a classic kern table, *ckern_table is set to NULL.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle.

validation_flags must be a bit-field from FT_VALIDATE_CKERNXXX (FT_VALIDATE_MS, FT_VALIDATE_APPLE, or FT_VALIDATE_CKERN). If the table does not match the selected dialect(s), the function reports the table as invalid (returns an error).
ckern_table must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
On success, *ckern_table points to a buffer that must later be freed using FT_ClassicKern_Free; if *ckern_table is NULL, the table does not exist in the font.
Callers must check the returned FT_Error; 0 indicates success.

functions.name: FT_ClassicKern_Free
functions.signature: void FT_ClassicKern_Free( FT_Face face, FT_Bytes table );
functions.description: Release a buffer previously returned by FT_ClassicKern_Validate via its ckern_table output. Intended solely for deallocating the classic kern validator’s allocated buffer.
requirements: Use only to free buffers that were produced by FT_ClassicKern_Validate.
face should be the same FT_Face (from the same FT_Library instance) that was used when obtaining the buffer (inferred from FreeType API patterns and the function signature).
Do not free such buffers with standard memory deallocation functions; use this API instead.

functions.name: FT_Stream_OpenGzip
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stream_OpenGzip( FT_Stream stream, FT_Stream source );
functions.description: Opens a new FreeType stream that wraps and transparently decompresses gzip-compressed data from an existing source stream. Typically used to read .gz-compressed font resources (e.g., .pcf.gz). The resulting stream can be passed to FreeType APIs that consume FT_Stream. Note: backward seeks reset the decompressor, which can negatively impact performance. Closing the gzip stream does not close the source stream. May be unavailable if FreeType was built without zlib support (returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature).
requirements: stream must be a valid, non-NULL FT_Stream handle provided by the caller to be initialized as the gzip stream.
source must be a valid, non-NULL FT_Stream that has been opened before calling this function.
The source stream must remain valid and open for the lifetime of the gzip stream.
Call FT_Stream_Close on the gzip stream when done; this will not close the source stream. The caller is responsible for closing the source stream separately.
Function returns an FT_Error; 0 indicates success. Callers must check the return value.
Feature requires FreeType built with zlib; otherwise the function may return FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature.

functions.name: FT_Gzip_Uncompress
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Gzip_Uncompress( FT_Memory memory, FT_Byte* output, FT_ULong* output_len, const FT_Byte* input, FT_ULong input_len );
functions.description: Decompresses gzip-compressed data from an input buffer into a caller-provided output buffer, modeled after zlib’s uncompress. The caller supplies an FT_Memory handle and an output buffer large enough to hold the entire uncompressed data. On input, *output_len is the total capacity of output; on success it is updated to the actual number of bytes written. May be unavailable if FreeType was built without zlib support (returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature).
requirements: memory must be a valid FreeType FT_Memory handle.
output must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer.
output_len must be non-NULL; on input it specifies the output buffer capacity in bytes and must be large enough to hold the full uncompressed data.
On return, *output_len is set to the number of bytes actually written to output.
input must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the compressed data buffer.
input_len must be the size in bytes of the input buffer.
Function returns an FT_Error; 0 indicates success. Callers must check the return value.
Feature requires FreeType built with zlib; otherwise the function may return FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature.

functions.name: FT_Library_SetLcdFilter
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Library_SetLcdFilter(FT_Library library, FT_LcdFilter filter)
functions.description: Selects the LCD subpixel filter used when rendering glyph bitmaps in FT_RENDER_MODE_LCD or FT_RENDER_MODE_LCD_V. Use FT_LCD_FILTER_NONE to disable, FT_LCD_FILTER_DEFAULT (enabled by default since 2.10.3), or other FT_LcdFilter presets. If the library was built without FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING, the call does nothing and returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle to an initialized FreeType library instance (target library instance).
filter must be a value from the FT_LcdFilter enumeration (e.g., FT_LCD_FILTER_NONE, FT_LCD_FILTER_DEFAULT, FT_LCD_FILTER_LIGHT, FT_LCD_FILTER_LEGACY, FT_LCD_FILTER_LEGACY1).
Callers must handle the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
If FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING is not defined in the build, the function returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature and has no effect.

functions.name: FT_Library_SetLcdFilterWeights
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Library_SetLcdFilterWeights(FT_Library library, unsigned char* weights)
functions.description: Enables LCD filtering with custom FIR weights instead of presets. Copies the first five bytes from weights as the filter taps in 1/256 units for subpixel-rendered bitmaps. If the library was built without FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING, the call does nothing and returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle to an initialized FreeType library instance.
weights must point to at least 5 readable bytes; the function copies the first five bytes.
Weights are interpreted as 1/256 units; caller is responsible for choosing values (no normalization enforced by this API).
Callers must handle the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
If FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING is not defined in the build, the function returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature and has no effect.

functions.name: FT_Library_SetLcdGeometry
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Library_SetLcdGeometry(FT_Library library, FT_Vector sub[3])
functions.description: Sets the default subpixel positions (geometry) used by Harmony LCD rendering by supplying three FT_Vector positions in 26.6 fractional pixel format. This controls how each color channel is shifted during rendering. In ClearType-style builds (FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING defined), this function does nothing and returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle to an initialized FreeType library instance.
sub must point to an array of exactly 3 FT_Vector entries, each expressed in 26.6 fractional pixel units; the function uses these to modify the defaults.
Callers must handle the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
If FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING is defined (ClearType-style), the function returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature and has no effect.

functions.name: FT_List_Find
functions.signature: FT_ListNode FT_List_Find(FT_List list, void* data);
functions.description: Finds and returns the list node that contains the given data pointer within the specified FreeType doubly-linked list. Use to locate an element's node for later manipulation (remove, move, etc.). Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: list must reference a valid, initialized FT_List (as defined in freetype.h).
data is the address of the listed object to search for.
Caller must handle a NULL return value when the object is not found.

functions.name: FT_List_Add
functions.signature: void FT_List_Add(FT_List list, FT_ListNode node);
functions.description: Appends the given node to the end (tail) of the specified list. Use to maintain insertion order where new elements are added at the back.
requirements: list must reference a valid, initialized FT_List.
node must be a valid FT_ListNode intended for this list.
Nodes added by this function are expected to have been dynamically allocated if they will later be finalized by FT_List_Finalize (per note in FT_List_Finalize).

functions.name: FT_List_Insert
functions.signature: void FT_List_Insert(FT_List list, FT_ListNode node);
functions.description: Inserts the given node at the head of the specified list. Use when you need stack-like or LRU-front insertion semantics.
requirements: list must reference a valid, initialized FT_List.
node must be a valid FT_ListNode intended for this list.
Nodes added by this function are expected to have been dynamically allocated if they will later be finalized by FT_List_Finalize (per note in FT_List_Finalize).

functions.name: FT_List_Remove
functions.signature: void FT_List_Remove(FT_List list, FT_ListNode node);
functions.description: Removes the specified node from the given list. This function does not verify that the node actually belongs to the list; it simply unlinks based on the node pointers.
requirements: list must reference a valid, initialized FT_List.
node must be a node that is currently in the specified list. The function does not check membership; passing a node not in the list may corrupt the list.
Caller is responsible for any lifecycle management of the removed node (this function only unlinks it; it does not destroy it).

functions.name: FT_List_Up
functions.signature: void FT_List_Up(FT_List list, FT_ListNode node);
functions.description: Moves the specified node to the head (top) of the list. Commonly used to maintain LRU lists by promoting recently used elements.
requirements: list must reference a valid, initialized FT_List.
node must be a node that is currently in the specified list.

functions.name: FT_List_Iterate
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_List_Iterate(FT_List list, FT_List_Iterator iterator, void* user);
functions.description: Traverses the list and calls the provided iterator callback for each node. Iteration stops immediately if the iterator returns a non-zero FT_Error. Returns the FT_Error from the last iterator call (zero on full success).
requirements: list must reference a valid, initialized FT_List.
iterator must be a valid function pointer of type FT_List_Iterator (FT_Error (*)(FT_ListNode, void*)).
Iterator return value controls traversal: returning non-zero stops iteration; caller should check the returned FT_Error from FT_List_Iterate.

functions.name: FT_List_Finalize
functions.signature: void FT_List_Finalize(FT_List list, FT_List_Destructor destroy, FT_Memory memory, void* user);
functions.description: Destroys all elements in the list and the list itself. For each element, optionally calls the provided destructor callback, then uses the given FT_Memory to deallocate. The user pointer is passed through to the destructor.
requirements: list must be a handle to the list to finalize.
destroy may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid function pointer of type FT_List_Destructor (void (*)(FT_Memory, void*, void*)).
memory must be a valid FT_Memory object that handles deallocation.
All nodes added by FT_List_Add or FT_List_Insert are expected to have been dynamically allocated (per the note); callers must ensure this prior to finalization.
After finalization, the list and its nodes must no longer be used by the caller.

functions.name: FT_Trace_Set_Level
functions.signature: void FT_Trace_Set_Level(const char* tracing_level);
functions.description: Sets FreeType’s per-component tracing level at runtime. Use this to control what FT_DEBUG_LOGGING emits without rebuilding. The argument is a string describing component:level pairs (for example, "any:7 memory:0"). If the library was not built with FT_DEBUG_LOGGING enabled, the call is a no-op.
requirements: tracing_level must point to a valid, NUL-terminated C string encoded in the format understood by FreeType’s tracer (e.g., component:level pairs like "any:7").
This function only has an effect if the library was compiled with FT_DEBUG_LOGGING; otherwise it does nothing.
The string must remain readable for the duration of the call (no additional lifetime requirements).

functions.name: FT_Trace_Set_Default_Level
functions.signature: void FT_Trace_Set_Default_Level(void);
functions.description: Resets tracing levels to the default (the value from the FT2_DEBUG environment variable, or to none if FT2_DEBUG is not set). Useful to undo custom trace settings at runtime. If FT_DEBUG_LOGGING is not enabled at build time, the call is a no-op.
requirements: This function only has an effect if the library was compiled with FT_DEBUG_LOGGING; otherwise it does nothing.

functions.name: FT_Set_Log_Handler
functions.signature: void FT_Set_Log_Handler(FT_Custom_Log_Handler handler);
functions.description: Installs a custom logging callback for tracing/debug messages. The handler receives the component name, a printf-like format string, and a va_list of arguments. Use this to redirect FreeType logging to your own sink (files, system logger, etc.). If FT_DEBUG_LOGGING is not enabled at build time, the call is a no-op.
requirements: handler must be a valid function pointer matching the FT_Custom_Log_Handler prototype: void (*)(const char* ft_component, const char* fmt, va_list args).
The function pointer supplied in handler must remain valid until it is replaced or until FT_Set_Default_Log_Handler is called.
The handler must correctly interpret fmt with the supplied va_list as a printf-style message.
This function only has an effect if the library was compiled with FT_DEBUG_LOGGING; otherwise it does nothing.

functions.name: FT_Set_Default_Log_Handler
functions.signature: void FT_Set_Default_Log_Handler(void);
functions.description: Restores FreeType’s built-in logging handler, undoing a prior FT_Set_Log_Handler call. If FT_DEBUG_LOGGING is not enabled at build time, the call is a no-op.
requirements: This function only has an effect if the library was compiled with FT_DEBUG_LOGGING; otherwise it does nothing.

functions.name: FT_Stream_OpenLZW
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stream_OpenLZW( FT_Stream stream, FT_Stream source );
functions.description: Opens an FT_Stream that transparently reads from an LZW-compressed source stream. Intended for reading LZW-compressed font files (e.g., *.pcf.Z). The function initializes the target stream (stream) to decode on-the-fly from the already-open source stream (source). Seeking backwards in the resulting stream is supported but inefficient because the decompressor is reset and data is re-decoded. If FreeType was built without LZW support, the function returns FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature.
requirements: source must be an already-open FreeType stream (opened before this call).
stream must be a valid FT_Stream object provided by the caller to receive the initialized LZW-decoding stream; it must not be closed or freed before calling FT_Stream_Close on it.
Calling FT_Stream_Close on stream does not close or affect source; the caller must manage and close source independently.
The function returns a FreeType error code; the caller must check for non-zero (failure), including FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature when LZW support is not built in.
Performance note: backward seeks on stream are allowed but are slow due to decompressor resets; callers should minimize backward seeking if performance-sensitive.
Memory ownership note: no stream objects are released to the heap by calling FT_Stream_Close on stream; the caller is responsible for lifetimes of both stream and source.

functions.name: FT_Get_Multi_Master
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Multi_Master(FT_Face face, FT_Multi_Master* amaster);
functions.description: Retrieve the variation (multiple master) descriptor of an Adobe Type 1 Multiple Master (MM) font. Not applicable to TrueType GX or OpenType Font Variations. The function fills the caller-provided FT_Multi_Master structure with axis and design information for the face.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face referring to an Adobe MM font (not TrueType GX or OpenType Font Variations)
amaster must be a non-null pointer to writable FT_Multi_Master storage supplied by the caller
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_MM_Var
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_MM_Var(FT_Face face, FT_MM_Var** amaster);
functions.description: Retrieve the unified variation descriptor (axes, named instances, etc.) for the given font. Works for Adobe MM, TrueType GX, and OpenType Font Variations. Allocates an FT_MM_Var that must be freed with FT_Done_MM_Var.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
amaster must be a non-null pointer to receive an allocated FT_MM_Var*
on success, the returned FT_MM_Var must be freed by calling FT_Done_MM_Var with the face's parent FT_Library
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Done_MM_Var
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Done_MM_Var(FT_Library library, FT_MM_Var* amaster);
functions.description: Free the FT_MM_Var structure previously allocated by FT_Get_MM_Var.
requirements: library must be the FT_Library used for the face when FT_Get_MM_Var created amaster
amaster must be a pointer previously returned by FT_Get_MM_Var (or NULL if no action is desired)
after a successful call, amaster must not be used again by the caller
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_MM_Design_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_MM_Design_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Long* coords);
functions.description: For Adobe MM fonts, select an interpolated design using design-space coordinates (Type 1 MM). This does not apply to TrueType GX or OpenType variations. Passing zero coords and NULL resets axes to defaults.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face for an Adobe MM font
if num_coords > 0, coords must point to at least num_coords FT_Long entries
if num_coords is larger than the number of axes, excess values are ignored
if num_coords is smaller than the number of axes, default values are used for remaining axes
to reset all axes to defaults, call with num_coords == 0 and coords == NULL (since 2.8.1)
if num_coords > 0, FT_FACE_FLAG_VARIATION is set; if num_coords == 0, the flag is unset (since 2.9)
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Fixed* coords);
functions.description: Select an interpolated design using design-space coordinates for any supported variation format (Adobe MM, TrueType GX, OpenType). For GX/OT, coordinates are 16.16 fixed; for Adobe MM, whole-number values are expected. Zero/NULL resets to the current named instance's defaults (or base font).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
if num_coords > 0, coords must point to at least num_coords FT_Fixed entries
if num_coords is larger than the number of axes, excess values are ignored
if num_coords is smaller than the number of axes, default values are used for remaining axes
for TrueType GX and OpenType, coordinates are 16.16 fixed-point; for Adobe MM, values should be integral (fractional part zero)
to reset to defaults, call with num_coords == 0 and coords == NULL (since 2.8.1)
‘Defaults’ are for the currently selected named instance or base font if none (since 2.9)
if num_coords > 0, FT_FACE_FLAG_VARIATION is set; if num_coords == 0, it is unset (since 2.9); it is also set if any provided coordinate differs from the default for its axis (since 2.14)
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_Var_Design_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Var_Design_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Fixed* coords);
functions.description: Retrieve the current design-space coordinates for the face. Works with all supported variation formats. Caller allocates the output array.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
coords must point to writable storage for at least num_coords FT_Fixed entries
if num_coords is larger than the number of axes, excess coords are set to 0
for TrueType GX and OpenType, returned values are 16.16 fixed; for Adobe MM, whole numbers (fractional part zero)
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_MM_Blend_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_MM_Blend_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Fixed* coords);
functions.description: Select an interpolated design using normalized (‘blend’) coordinates. For Adobe MM the valid range is [0,1] (16.16). For TrueType GX and OpenType the valid range is [-1,1] (16.16). Zero/NULL resets to defaults. Sets or clears the variation flag based on inputs and default position status.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
if num_coords > 0, coords must point to at least num_coords FT_Fixed entries
each coordinate must be within 0..1.0 (Adobe MM) or -1.0..1.0 (TrueType GX/OpenType), expressed as 16.16 fixed-point
if num_coords is larger than the number of axes, excess values are ignored
if num_coords is smaller than the number of axes, default values are used for remaining axes
to reset to defaults, call with num_coords == 0 and coords == NULL (since 2.8.1)
‘Defaults’ use the currently selected named instance or base font if none (since 2.9)
if num_coords > 0, FT_FACE_FLAG_VARIATION is set; if num_coords == 0, it is unset (since 2.9); it is also set if any coordinate differs from the default for its axis (since 2.14)
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_MM_Blend_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_MM_Blend_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Fixed* coords);
functions.description: Retrieve the current normalized (‘blend’) coordinates for the face. Caller allocates the output array. Excess requested entries are set to 0.5 for Adobe MM and 0 for TrueType GX/OpenType.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
coords must point to writable storage for at least num_coords FT_Fixed entries
if num_coords is larger than the number of axes, excess entries are set to 0.5 (Adobe MM) or 0 (TrueType GX/OpenType)
returned values are 16.16 fixed-point
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Var_Blend_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_Var_Blend_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Fixed* coords);
functions.description: Alias of FT_Set_MM_Blend_Coordinates; selects an interpolated design using normalized coordinates for any supported variation format. See FT_Set_MM_Blend_Coordinates for details.
requirements: same requirements as FT_Set_MM_Blend_Coordinates

functions.name: FT_Get_Var_Blend_Coordinates
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Var_Blend_Coordinates(FT_Face face, FT_UInt num_coords, FT_Fixed* coords);
functions.description: Alias of FT_Get_MM_Blend_Coordinates; retrieves the current normalized coordinates. See FT_Get_MM_Blend_Coordinates for details.
requirements: same requirements as FT_Get_MM_Blend_Coordinates

functions.name: FT_Set_MM_WeightVector
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_MM_WeightVector(FT_Face face, FT_UInt len, FT_Fixed* weightvector);
functions.description: For Adobe MM fonts, directly set the design’s weight vector to choose an interpolated instance. len specifies how many entries to read. len==0 resets to defaults and unsets the variation flag. Values are 16.16 fixed-point; they are not enforced to sum to 1.0.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face for an Adobe MM font
if len > 0, weightvector must point to at least len FT_Fixed entries
if len is larger than the number of designs, extra values are ignored
if len is smaller than the number of designs, remaining values are set to 0
Adobe MM fonts limit the number of designs (and thus weight vector length) to 16 elements
if len > 0, FT_FACE_FLAG_VARIATION is set; if len == 0, the flag is unset and the weight vector resets to defaults
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_MM_WeightVector
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_MM_WeightVector(FT_Face face, FT_UInt* len, FT_Fixed* weightvector);
functions.description: For Adobe MM fonts, retrieve the current weight vector. Caller provides an array and its capacity via *len; on success, *len is set to the number of designs written. If capacity is too small, returns FT_Err_Invalid_Argument and sets *len to the required size.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face for an Adobe MM font
len must be a non-null pointer; on input it is the capacity of weightvector; on output it is set to the number of designs (required/written)
weightvector must point to writable storage for at least *len FT_Fixed entries on successful completion
if provided array size is less than the number of designs, function returns FT_Err_Invalid_Argument and sets *len to required size
if provided array size is greater than the number of designs, remaining entries are set to 0
Adobe MM fonts limit the number of designs (and thus weight vector length) to 16 elements
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error (including FT_Err_Invalid_Argument) on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_Var_Axis_Flags
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Var_Axis_Flags(FT_MM_Var* master, FT_UInt axis_index, FT_UInt* flags);
functions.description: Return the flags field of an OpenType Variation Axis Record for the given axis in the variation descriptor. For Adobe MM fonts, flags is always zero.
requirements: master must be a valid pointer to an FT_MM_Var obtained from FT_Get_MM_Var
axis_index must designate an existing axis (0 <= axis_index < master->num_axis)
flags must be a non-null pointer to receive the bitfield (e.g., FT_VAR_AXIS_FLAG_HIDDEN)
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Set_Named_Instance
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Set_Named_Instance(FT_Face face, FT_UInt instance_index);
functions.description: Select or change the current named instance for a variation-capable face. Pass 0 to clear and access the base font without a named instance. Resets any applied variation and clears the face’s variation flag. For Adobe MM fonts, resets to the default instance.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
instance_index == 0 switches to no named instance; otherwise it is the 1-based index of the requested named instance
calling this resets any variation coordinates and clears FT_FACE_FLAG_VARIATION
for faces without named instances, using a non-zero index is invalid (error returned) though exact bounds are not specified in this header
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Get_Default_Named_Instance
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Default_Named_Instance(FT_Face face, FT_UInt* instance_index);
functions.description: Retrieve the index of the default named instance suitable for FT_Set_Named_Instance. FreeType synthesizes a default named instance if the font lacks one. For Adobe MM fonts, returns 0.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face
instance_index must be a non-null pointer to receive the default instance index
for Adobe MM fonts, *instance_index is always set to 0
returns 0 on success; non-zero FT_Error on failure

functions.name: FT_Add_Module
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Add_Module(FT_Library library, const FT_Module_Class* clazz);
functions.description: Registers a new module (driver/renderer/etc.) with a given FreeType library instance. Used to add internal or external modules at runtime; typically called after creating a library with FT_New_Library (or rarely to add alternatives). Returns 0 on success, non-zero FT_Error on failure.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
clazz must point to a valid FT_Module_Class descriptor for the module.
Fails if a module with the same module_name is already present.
Fails if the module’s module_requires version exceeds the FreeType version of the library.

functions.name: FT_Get_Module
functions.signature: FT_Module FT_Get_Module(FT_Library library, const char* module_name);
functions.description: Looks up a module by ASCII name in the given library and returns its handle, or 0 if not found. Useful for querying a module’s interfaces or properties.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
module_name must be a valid, null-terminated ASCII string corresponding to the module’s module_name.

functions.name: FT_Remove_Module
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Remove_Module(FT_Library library, FT_Module module);
functions.description: Unregisters and destroys a module from the specified library instance. On success, the module object is destroyed. Returns 0 on success, non-zero FT_Error otherwise.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
module must be a valid FT_Module belonging to the given library.
On success the module handle becomes invalid after the call (the module is destroyed).

functions.name: FT_Property_Set
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Property_Set(FT_Library library, const FT_String* module_name, const FT_String* property_name, const void* value);
functions.description: Sets a named property of a module to a new value. Only some modules expose properties; property value types and semantics are module-specific (see the module’s property documentation). Returns 0 on success.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
module_name must be a valid module name (e.g., obtainable via FT_FACE_DRIVER_NAME).
property_name must be a valid property for the specified module.
value must point to a correctly typed object for the property as defined by the module documentation.
If module_name, property_name, or value is invalid for the property, the function returns an error.
Changing module properties does not update the FreeType Cache automatically; callers should reset the cache via FTC_Manager_Reset if properties change after FTC_Manager_New.

functions.name: FT_Property_Get
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Property_Get(FT_Library library, const FT_String* module_name, const FT_String* property_name, void* value);
functions.description: Retrieves the current value of a named property of a module and writes it to the caller-provided storage pointed to by value. Only some modules expose properties; value’s expected type and layout are module-specific. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
module_name must be a valid module name.
property_name must be a valid property for the specified module.
value must point to writable storage of the correct type/size for the property as defined by the module documentation.
Returns an error if module_name/property_name is invalid or if value is not appropriate for the property.
Cannot be used to retrieve properties of the FreeType Cache sub-system; use FTC_Property_Get instead.

functions.name: FT_Set_Default_Properties
functions.signature: void FT_Set_Default_Properties(FT_Library library);
functions.description: If built with FT_CONFIG_OPTION_ENVIRONMENT_PROPERTIES, reads the FREETYPE_PROPERTIES environment variable and applies listed module properties to the given library. Otherwise it does nothing.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
Only effective if the library was compiled with FT_CONFIG_OPTION_ENVIRONMENT_PROPERTIES enabled.
The FREETYPE_PROPERTIES environment variable must follow the documented syntax: <module>:<property>=<value> entries separated by whitespace.

functions.name: FT_Reference_Library
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Reference_Library(FT_Library library);
functions.description: Increments the reference counter of the FT_Library. FT_Done_Library only destroys the library when the counter drops to 1 and then is decremented; otherwise it just decrements the counter. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle created by FT_Init_FreeType or FT_New_Library.
Each successful call increases the library’s reference count; callers must later balance with FT_Done_Library calls to avoid leaks.

functions.name: FT_New_Library
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_New_Library(FT_Memory memory, FT_Library* alibrary);
functions.description: Creates a new FreeType library instance using the provided FT_Memory allocator, allowing custom memory management. Typically followed by FT_Add_Default_Modules (or manual FT_Add_Module calls) and FT_Set_Default_Properties. Returns 0 on success and stores the new handle in *alibrary.
requirements: memory must be a valid FT_Memory object whose lifetime spans the entire lifetime of the created FT_Library.
alibrary must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created FT_Library handle.
After creation, callers should add modules (FT_Add_Default_Modules or FT_Add_Module) and optionally apply properties (FT_Set_Default_Properties) before general use.
Destroy the library with FT_Done_Library (not FT_Done_FreeType).
Reference counting applies as described for FT_Reference_Library.

functions.name: FT_Done_Library
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Done_Library(FT_Library library);
functions.description: Disposes of a library object: closes drivers and releases resources. Honors the library’s reference count: destroys only if the counter is 1; otherwise decrements it. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
Should be used to destroy libraries created by FT_New_Library (and also libraries from FT_Init_FreeType).
Library destruction behavior depends on the reference count (see FT_Reference_Library).

functions.name: FT_Set_Debug_Hook
functions.signature: void FT_Set_Debug_Hook(FT_Library library, FT_UInt hook_index, FT_DebugHook_Func debug_hook);
functions.description: Installs a debug hook function for a font interpreter (e.g., TrueType). Intended for debugging/tracing the interpreter by replacing/wrapping its main loop. Public API but typically requires access to FreeType internal headers to be useful.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
hook_index should be one of the defined indices (e.g., FT_DEBUG_HOOK_TRUETYPE).
Currently there are four available hook slots; only the TrueType interpreter hook is defined.
debug_hook must be a valid function pointer matching FT_DebugHook_Func or NULL to clear (NULL behavior not explicitly documented; caller should consult implementation if needed).

functions.name: FT_Add_Default_Modules
functions.signature: void FT_Add_Default_Modules(FT_Library library);
functions.description: Registers the standard set of FreeType drivers/modules into the given library. Typically used after creating a library with FT_New_Library (especially when using a custom memory manager).
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
Primarily intended for libraries created with FT_New_Library; for FT_Init_FreeType, modules are already added.

functions.name: FT_Get_TrueType_Engine_Type
functions.signature: FT_TrueTypeEngineType FT_Get_TrueType_Engine_Type(FT_Library library);
functions.description: Returns which TrueType bytecode engine level the library supports (none or patented-full set). Use to query interpreter availability/capabilities at runtime.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.

functions.name: FT_OpenType_Validate
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_OpenType_Validate( FT_Face face, FT_UInt validation_flags, FT_Bytes* BASE_table, FT_Bytes* GDEF_table, FT_Bytes* GPOS_table, FT_Bytes* GSUB_table, FT_Bytes* JSTF_table );
functions.description: Validate selected OpenType layout tables (BASE, GDEF, GPOS, GSUB, JSTF, MATH) in an FT_Face and, for requested tables, return allocated buffers pointing to the validated raw table data. Intended to let higher-level layout engines use the tables without performing their own offset/index checks. Returns 0 on success (FT_Error). After use, free any non-NULL returned table buffers with FT_OpenType_Free. Only works on OpenType fonts; non-OpenType faces return an error. Tables not present in the font or not requested for validation will yield NULL outputs.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face loaded by FreeType and must reference an OpenType font; otherwise the function returns an error.

validation_flags is a bit-field selecting which tables to validate; use FT_VALIDATE_BASE, FT_VALIDATE_GDEF, FT_VALIDATE_GPOS, FT_VALIDATE_GSUB, FT_VALIDATE_JSTF, FT_VALIDATE_MATH, or their combination (e.g., FT_VALIDATE_OT).

For each output parameter (BASE_table, GDEF_table, GPOS_table, GSUB_table, JSTF_table), provide a valid FT_Bytes* location to receive the result for any table you request; outputs may be set to NULL if the table is absent or not requested.
On success, any non-NULL returned table buffer must be released with FT_OpenType_Free using the same face and the returned FT_Bytes pointer.
Callers must check the returned FT_Error; a non-zero value indicates failure and outputs should not be used except as documented by FreeType.
Do not attempt to free or modify returned buffers by any means other than FT_OpenType_Free.

functions.name: FT_OpenType_Free
functions.signature: void FT_OpenType_Free( FT_Face face, FT_Bytes table );
functions.description: Free a buffer previously returned by FT_OpenType_Validate for an OpenType table associated with the given FT_Face. Use this only for deallocating those specific buffers.
requirements: face must be the same FT_Face used when obtaining the table buffer via FT_OpenType_Validate.
table must be a pointer previously returned by FT_OpenType_Validate; do not pass arbitrary pointers.
Use this function only to free buffers allocated by FT_OpenType_Validate; do not use it for other memory.
Do not use the buffer after calling FT_OpenType_Free (dangling pointer).

functions.name: FT_Outline_Decompose
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Decompose( FT_Outline* outline, const FT_Outline_Funcs* func_interface, void* user );
functions.description: Decomposes an outline into a sequence of path operations (move-to, line-to, conic-to, cubic-to), invoking the user-supplied emitters in func_interface for each segment. The user pointer is passed through to each emitter to maintain state. Returns 0 on success. Degenerate segments and empty outlines may be reported; callers should filter if needed.
requirements: outline must point to a valid FT_Outline (empty outlines are allowed; function may do nothing and still succeed).
func_interface must point to a valid FT_Outline_Funcs table with appropriate callbacks for the outline’s content.
user is passed through to callbacks and may be NULL.
Caller should be prepared to receive degenerate contours/segments/Bezier arcs from callbacks.
The function returns a FreeType error code; caller must check for non-zero to detect failure.

functions.name: FT_Outline_New
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_New( FT_Library library, FT_UInt numPoints, FT_Int numContours, FT_Outline* anoutline );
functions.description: Creates a new, empty FT_Outline with capacity for the specified number of points and contours. Memory is allocated using the given library’s allocator. Returns 0 on success and places the allocated outline in *anoutline.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle (used for allocation).
numPoints must be <= 0xFFFF (65535).
numContours must be in the range [0, numPoints].
anoutline must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated outline handle.
Caller must check the returned error code before using *anoutline.
Destroy the outline later with FT_Outline_Done using the same library handle.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Done
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Done( FT_Library library, FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Destroys an FT_Outline previously created by FT_Outline_New, releasing memory via the given library’s allocator. Returns 0 on success. If the outline’s owner flag is not set, only the descriptor is released.
requirements: library must be the FT_Library used to allocate the outline.
outline must point to an outline created with FT_Outline_New (or otherwise compatible with this deallocator).
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Check
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Check( FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Validates the structural contents of an FT_Outline descriptor. Empty outlines and outlines with a single point are considered valid. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: outline must point to an FT_Outline to be checked (may be empty or contain a single point).
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Get_CBox
functions.signature: void FT_Outline_Get_CBox( const FT_Outline* outline, FT_BBox* acbox );
functions.description: Computes the control box (CBox) of an outline, which encloses all points including Bezier control points. It is fast but may be slightly larger than the exact bounding box for some glyphs. Writes the box to *acbox.
requirements: outline must point to a valid source outline.
acbox must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting FT_BBox.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Translate
functions.signature: void FT_Outline_Translate( const FT_Outline* outline, FT_Pos xOffset, FT_Pos yOffset );
functions.description: Applies a translation by (xOffset, yOffset) to the points of an outline. Intended to shift the outline’s geometry in-place.
requirements: outline must point to the target outline to be translated.
xOffset and yOffset are in the outline’s FT_Pos units; no specific range restrictions stated.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Copy
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Copy( const FT_Outline* source, FT_Outline* target );
functions.description: Copies the content of one outline into another. Both outlines must already have identical sizes (same number of points and contours). Returns 0 on success.
requirements: source must point to a valid source outline.
target must point to a valid target outline.
source and target must have the same sizes (number of points and number of contours) before calling.
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Transform
functions.signature: void FT_Outline_Transform( const FT_Outline* outline, const FT_Matrix* matrix );
functions.description: Applies a 2×2 linear transformation (e.g., rotate, slant, flip) to all points in an outline using the provided FT_Matrix. To translate, use FT_Outline_Translate separately.
requirements: outline must point to the target outline to be transformed.
matrix must point to a valid FT_Matrix describing the transform.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Embolden
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Embolden( FT_Outline* outline, FT_Pos strength );
functions.description: Thickens or thins an outline by an amount related to strength in 26.6 pixel units. The resulting outline becomes up to ~4×strength wider and taller; negative strength is allowed to reduce thickness. Point count is unchanged; certain shapes (e.g., acute angles/intersections) may be handled imperfectly. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: outline must point to the target outline to be emboldened.
strength is expressed in 26.6 pixel format; may be negative.
Caller must check the returned error code.
For ‘better’ metrics after modification, use FT_Outline_Get_CBox or FT_Outline_Get_BBox (advisory note, not a strict requirement).

functions.name: FT_Outline_EmboldenXY
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_EmboldenXY( FT_Outline* outline, FT_Pos xstrength, FT_Pos ystrength );
functions.description: Anisotropically emboldens an outline: increases width by xstrength and height by ystrength (26.6 pixel units). Otherwise similar to FT_Outline_Embolden. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: outline must point to the target outline to be emboldened.
xstrength and ystrength are expressed in 26.6 pixel format; may be negative.
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Reverse
functions.signature: void FT_Outline_Reverse( FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Reverses the drawing direction of all contours in an outline, toggling the FT_OUTLINE_REVERSE_FILL flag to maintain fill semantics for mirrored glyphs. Intended for specialized use.
requirements: outline must point to the target outline to be reversed.
Caller should only use this if they understand the effect on fill conventions (advisory note from documentation).

functions.name: FT_Outline_Get_Bitmap
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Get_Bitmap( FT_Library library, FT_Outline* outline, const FT_Bitmap* abitmap );
functions.description: Renders an outline into an existing bitmap, OR-ing the outline’s coverage into the target. Uses the default glyph raster. Returns 0 on success. This function does not create the bitmap; the caller must provide a properly initialized bitmap object.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
outline must point to the source outline descriptor.
abitmap must point to a pre-initialized bitmap descriptor that provides a valid target surface; the function will not allocate it.
The value of abitmap->num_grays is ignored when using the gray raster; for fewer than 256 grays, use FT_Outline_Render directly.
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Render
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Outline_Render( FT_Library library, FT_Outline* outline, FT_Raster_Params* params );
functions.description: Renders an outline using the current scan converter, configured via FT_Raster_Params. The function sets params->source to the outline. Either params->target must point to a preallocated bitmap, or FT_RASTER_FLAG_DIRECT must be set to enable direct rendering. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: library must be a valid FT_Library handle.
outline must point to the source outline descriptor.
params must point to a valid FT_Raster_Params structure.
params->source is ignored on input and will be set to the outline by this function.
Either params->target must be a valid preallocated bitmap, or FT_RASTER_FLAG_DIRECT must be set in params->flags.
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: FT_Outline_Get_Orientation
functions.signature: FT_Orientation FT_Outline_Get_Orientation( FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Analyzes an outline’s total signed area to determine contour fill orientation. Returns FT_ORIENTATION_POSTSCRIPT for positive (clockwise) area, FT_ORIENTATION_TRUETYPE for negative (counter-clockwise) area. Empty outlines return FT_ORIENTATION_TRUETYPE.
requirements: outline must point to the source outline.
Caller should be aware that empty outlines yield FT_ORIENTATION_TRUETYPE.

functions.name: FT_Get_PFR_Metrics
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_PFR_Metrics(FT_Face face, FT_UInt* aoutline_resolution, FT_UInt* ametrics_resolution, FT_Fixed* ametrics_x_scale, FT_Fixed* ametrics_y_scale)
functions.description: Returns the outline and metrics resolutions for a PFR (TrueDoc) face, along with 16.16 fixed-point x/y metric scales. Intended for callers that need original PFR metrics rather than standard outline units. If face is not a PFR face, the function returns an error code but still provides valid values (falling back to the face’s standard metrics). Optional output pointers may be NULL to skip specific results.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle (may be non-PFR; in that case an error is returned, but outputs are still valid).
aoutline_resolution may be NULL if the outline resolution is not needed; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to FT_UInt.
ametrics_resolution may be NULL if the metrics resolution is not needed; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to FT_UInt.
ametrics_x_scale may be NULL if the horizontal metrics scale is not needed; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to FT_Fixed (16.16).
ametrics_y_scale may be NULL if the vertical metrics scale is not needed; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to FT_Fixed (16.16).
Caller must check the returned FT_Error; even on error, output values are documented to be valid and may be used.

functions.name: FT_Get_PFR_Kerning
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_PFR_Kerning(FT_Face face, FT_UInt left, FT_UInt right, FT_Vector* avector)
functions.description: Returns the kerning vector between two glyph indices for a PFR face, in original PFR metrics units (not outline units). Use the x_scale/y_scale from FT_Get_PFR_Metrics to convert to device subpixels. Unlike FT_Get_Kerning(… FT_KERNING_UNSCALED), this does not convert to outline units.
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle for the font to query (PFR expected for meaningful results).
left must be a glyph index in the face (FT_UInt).
right must be a glyph index in the face (FT_UInt).
avector must be a non-NULL pointer to an FT_Vector to receive the kerning vector.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error before using the result.
If device-space values are needed, caller should scale the returned vector using the x_scale/y_scale from FT_Get_PFR_Metrics.

functions.name: FT_Get_PFR_Advance
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_PFR_Advance(FT_Face face, FT_UInt gindex, FT_Pos* aadvance)
functions.description: Returns the advance width of the specified glyph from a PFR face in original PFR metrics units. Use x_scale or y_scale from FT_Get_PFR_Metrics to convert to device subpixels (1/64 pixel units).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle for the font to query (PFR expected for meaningful results).
gindex must be a glyph index in the face (FT_UInt).
aadvance must be a non-NULL pointer to FT_Pos to receive the advance value.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error before using the result.
If device-space values are needed, caller should scale the returned advance using the appropriate scale from FT_Get_PFR_Metrics.

functions.name: FT_Get_Renderer
functions.signature:
FT_Renderer FT_Get_Renderer( FT_Library       library,
                   FT_Glyph_Format  format );
functions.description: Retrieve the current renderer registered in the given FreeType library that handles the specified glyph format. Typical usage: pass a valid FT_Library and a FT_Glyph_Format (e.g., FT_GLYPH_FORMAT_OUTLINE) and use the returned FT_Renderer (or NULL if none is available).
requirements: library must be a valid, initialized FT_Library handle (for example, created by FT_Init_FreeType).
format must be a valid FT_Glyph_Format value supported by FreeType.
Caller must handle the possibility of a NULL return (no renderer found for the given format).

functions.name: FT_Set_Renderer
functions.signature:
FT_Error FT_Set_Renderer( FT_Library     library,
                   FT_Renderer    renderer,
                   FT_UInt        num_params,
                   FT_Parameter*  parameters );
functions.description: Set the current renderer to use in the specified FreeType library and optionally pass renderer-specific mode parameters. On success, this renderer will be used to convert glyph images of its known format into bitmaps; renderers for other formats remain unchanged. Currently, FreeType renderers do not consume parameters, so pass NULL.
requirements: library must be a valid, initialized FT_Library handle.
renderer must be a valid FT_Renderer associated with the library and the glyph format it handles.
parameters should be NULL because currently no FreeType renderer module uses additional parameters.
If parameters is NULL, num_params should be 0 (to match the absence of parameters).
Return value is an FT_Error; callers must check for non-zero errors (0 means success).

functions.name: FT_New_Size
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_New_Size(FT_Face face, FT_Size* size);
functions.description: Create a new size object associated with the given FreeType face. Use this to maintain multiple pixel sizes for the same face. The created size does not become active automatically; call FT_Activate_Size to make it the current size for loading and rendering glyphs. On success, the new size handle is stored in *size and must later be released with FT_Done_Size (or implicitly via FT_Done_Face).
requirements: face must be a valid FT_Face handle (typically obtained from FT_New_Face) and remain alive for the lifetime of the created size.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created FT_Size handle.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error; a value of 0 indicates success.
The new size is not active by default; the caller must call FT_Activate_Size before relying on it for operations like FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes, FT_Set_Char_Size, FT_Load_Glyph, or FT_Load_Char.
On success, the returned FT_Size must be released exactly once with FT_Done_Size, unless the parent face is destroyed with FT_Done_Face (which discards all sizes automatically).

functions.name: FT_Done_Size
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Done_Size(FT_Size size);
functions.description: Dispose of (discard) a previously created size object. This releases resources associated with the size. Destroying a face with FT_Done_Face also discards all of its sizes, so explicit calls to FT_Done_Size are not needed in that case.
requirements: size must be a valid FT_Size handle previously created (e.g., by FT_New_Size) and not already destroyed.
After a successful call, the size handle must not be used again.
If the parent face has already been destroyed with FT_Done_Face, do not call FT_Done_Size for its sizes (they are discarded automatically).
Caller must check the returned FT_Error; a value of 0 indicates success.

functions.name: FT_Activate_Size
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Activate_Size(FT_Size size);
functions.description: Make the specified size object the active size for its parent face. Subsequent glyph loading and size-dependent operations for that face use this size (and the face->size field is updated accordingly). Use when managing multiple sizes on the same face.
requirements: size must be a valid FT_Size handle that was previously created and is associated with some FT_Face.
The parent face of size must still be valid when activating the size.
Caller must check the returned FT_Error; a value of 0 indicates success.

functions.name: FT_Get_Sfnt_Name_Count
functions.signature: FT_UInt FT_Get_Sfnt_Name_Count(FT_Face face);
functions.description: Returns the number of name records in the SFNT 'name' table of the given face. Use this to bound indices passed to FT_Get_Sfnt_Name. Note: availability depends on FreeType being built with TT_CONFIG_OPTION_SFNT_NAMES enabled.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face obtained from FreeType (non-NULL).
Callers should use the returned count to ensure indices passed to FT_Get_Sfnt_Name are within [0, count-1].
Function relies on TT_CONFIG_OPTION_SFNT_NAMES being enabled at build time; otherwise the feature is unavailable (behavior is implementation-defined in this header).

functions.name: FT_Get_Sfnt_Name
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Sfnt_Name(FT_Face face, FT_UInt idx, FT_SfntName* aname);
functions.description: Retrieves the SFNT 'name' table entry at the given index and fills an FT_SfntName structure describing the record. Intended usage: first call FT_Get_Sfnt_Name_Count to get the total number of records, then iterate indices to locate entries matching desired platform/encoding/name ID. The returned string is not NUL-terminated and is owned by FreeType (freed when the face is destroyed).
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face (non-NULL).
idx must be in the range [0, FT_Get_Sfnt_Name_Count(face) - 1].
aname must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for an FT_SfntName.
The string in the returned FT_SfntName is not NUL-terminated; callers must use string_len to process it.
Callers must not free or modify aname->string; it is managed by FreeType and released when FT_Done_Face is called.
Function returns FT_Error; 0 means success, non-zero indicates failure (e.g., unsupported feature or invalid index).
Feature requires FreeType to be built with TT_CONFIG_OPTION_SFNT_NAMES enabled; otherwise the function returns an error.

functions.name: FT_Get_Sfnt_LangTag
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Get_Sfnt_LangTag(FT_Face face, FT_UInt langID, FT_SfntLangTag* alangTag);
functions.description: Retrieves the language tag string associated with a language ID from a format-1 SFNT 'name' table. The returned string is UTF-16BE and not NUL-terminated; it is owned by FreeType and freed with the face. Use language IDs (>= 0x8000) obtained from FT_Get_Sfnt_Name.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized FT_Face (non-NULL).
alangTag must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for an FT_SfntLangTag.
langID must be a value larger than 0x8000 as returned by FT_Get_Sfnt_Name for format-1 'name' tables; otherwise FT_Err_Invalid_Argument may be returned.
Only 'name' table format 1 supports language tags; if the face uses format 0, the function returns FT_Err_Invalid_Table.
The string in the returned FT_SfntLangTag is UTF-16BE and not NUL-terminated; callers must use string_len to process it appropriately.
Callers must not free or modify alangTag->string; it is managed by FreeType and released when FT_Done_Face is called.
Function returns FT_Error; 0 means success, non-zero indicates failure.
Feature requires FreeType to be built with TT_CONFIG_OPTION_SFNT_NAMES enabled; otherwise the function returns an error.

functions.name: FT_Outline_GetInsideBorder
functions.signature: FT_StrokerBorder FT_Outline_GetInsideBorder( FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Return which stroker border corresponds to the inside of the given outline. Intended to help choose FT_STROKER_BORDER_LEFT or RIGHT when extracting a stroked outline’s inside border. Returns FT_STROKER_BORDER_RIGHT for empty or invalid outlines.
requirements: outline must point to a valid FT_Outline structure; empty or invalid outlines yield FT_STROKER_BORDER_RIGHT (per docs).
No allocation or output buffers are required; the function simply returns an enum value.

functions.name: FT_Outline_GetOutsideBorder
functions.signature: FT_StrokerBorder FT_Outline_GetOutsideBorder( FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Return which stroker border corresponds to the outside of the given outline. Intended to help choose FT_STROKER_BORDER_LEFT or RIGHT when extracting a stroked outline’s outside border. Returns FT_STROKER_BORDER_LEFT for empty or invalid outlines.
requirements: outline must point to a valid FT_Outline structure; empty or invalid outlines yield FT_STROKER_BORDER_LEFT (per docs).
No allocation or output buffers are required; the function simply returns an enum value.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_New
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_New( FT_Library library, FT_Stroker* astroker );
functions.description: Create a new path stroker associated with the given FreeType library. On success, stores the handle in *astroker.
requirements: library must be a valid, initialized FT_Library.
astroker must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created FT_Stroker; set to NULL on error (per docs).
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_Set
functions.signature: void FT_Stroker_Set( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Fixed radius, FT_Stroker_LineCap line_cap, FT_Stroker_LineJoin line_join, FT_Fixed miter_limit );
functions.description: Reset a stroker’s attributes: stroke radius, cap, join, and miter limit (16.16 fixed). Automatically rewinds the stroker for new input.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
radius is in the same units as outline coordinates (typically font units).
miter_limit is a 16.16 fixed-point value; the product miter_limit * radius controls spike length for miter joins (per docs).
This call implicitly performs FT_Stroker_Rewind; no need to rewind separately immediately after calling.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_Rewind
functions.signature: void FT_Stroker_Rewind( FT_Stroker stroker );
functions.description: Reset the stroker’s internal state without changing its attributes, preparing it to accept a new path (manual API) or to be used by ParseOutline.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
Call before beginning a new series of FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath/EndSubPath calls if reusing the stroker.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_ParseOutline
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_ParseOutline( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Outline* outline, FT_Bool opened );
functions.description: Convenience routine to feed a whole FT_Outline into the stroker. If opened==0, treats it as a closed path and generates left/right borders; if opened==1, treats as an open path and generates a single stroke border. Automatically rewinds the stroker.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
outline must point to a valid FT_Outline to parse.
opened must be 0 (closed) or 1 (open) semantics; affects number of borders generated.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
This call implicitly performs FT_Stroker_Rewind before parsing.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Vector* to, FT_Bool open );
functions.description: Start a new sub-path at the specified start point, for manually feeding segments to the stroker (use when not using FT_Stroker_ParseOutline).
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
to must point to a valid FT_Vector start position.
open must be 0 (closed sub-path) or 1 (open sub-path).
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
Typically call after FT_Stroker_Rewind and before any LineTo/ConicTo/CubicTo calls for this sub-path.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_EndSubPath
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_EndSubPath( FT_Stroker stroker );
functions.description: End the current sub-path previously begun with FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath. If the sub-path is closed, this may add a line back to the start point as needed.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
Must be called after a matching FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath for the current sub-path.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_LineTo
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_LineTo( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Vector* to );
functions.description: Append a straight line segment from the current point to the destination point in the stroker’s current sub-path.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
Must be called between FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath and FT_Stroker_EndSubPath for an active sub-path.
to must point to a valid FT_Vector destination point.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_ConicTo
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_ConicTo( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Vector* control, FT_Vector* to );
functions.description: Append a quadratic (conic) Bézier segment from the current point to the destination, using the given control point, in the current sub-path.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
Must be called between FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath and FT_Stroker_EndSubPath for an active sub-path.
control must point to a valid FT_Vector control point.
to must point to a valid FT_Vector destination point.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_CubicTo
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_CubicTo( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Vector* control1, FT_Vector* control2, FT_Vector* to );
functions.description: Append a cubic Bézier segment from the current point to the destination, using the two control points, in the current sub-path.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
Must be called between FT_Stroker_BeginSubPath and FT_Stroker_EndSubPath for an active sub-path.
control1 and control2 must each point to valid FT_Vector control points.
to must point to a valid FT_Vector destination point.
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_GetBorderCounts
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_GetBorderCounts( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_StrokerBorder border, FT_UInt* anum_points, FT_UInt* anum_contours );
functions.description: Return the number of points and contours required to export the specified border (or stroke) produced by the stroker, after feeding paths.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
border must be FT_STROKER_BORDER_LEFT or FT_STROKER_BORDER_RIGHT.
anum_points and anum_contours must be non-NULL pointers to receive counts.
Should be called after finishing parsing paths (via ParseOutline or manual Begin/Line/…/End).
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_ExportBorder
functions.signature: void FT_Stroker_ExportBorder( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_StrokerBorder border, FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Append the generated points/contours for the given border to the caller-supplied FT_Outline. Does not resize the outline arrays; it only appends.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
border must be FT_STROKER_BORDER_LEFT or FT_STROKER_BORDER_RIGHT.
outline must be a valid FT_Outline with enough capacity to receive appended points/contours.
Caller should first call FT_Stroker_GetBorderCounts to size/ensure capacity (per docs).
Appends to existing outline data; caller is responsible for managing outline->points/tags/contours buffers and counts.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_GetCounts
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Stroker_GetCounts( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_UInt* anum_points, FT_UInt* anum_contours );
functions.description: Return the number of points and contours required to export all borders from the stroked path, after feeding paths.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
anum_points and anum_contours must be non-NULL pointers to receive counts.
Should be called after finishing parsing paths (via ParseOutline or manual Begin/Line/…/End).
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_Export
functions.signature: void FT_Stroker_Export( FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Outline* outline );
functions.description: Append all generated borders to the caller-supplied FT_Outline. Does not resize the outline arrays; it only appends.
requirements: stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker.
outline must be a valid FT_Outline with enough capacity to receive all appended points/contours.
Caller should first call FT_Stroker_GetCounts to size/ensure capacity (per docs).
Appends to existing outline data; caller is responsible for managing outline buffers and counts.

functions.name: FT_Stroker_Done
functions.signature: void FT_Stroker_Done( FT_Stroker stroker );
functions.description: Destroy a stroker object and release its resources. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: stroker may be NULL (no effect) or a valid FT_Stroker to be destroyed.
After this call, the stroker handle must not be used.

functions.name: FT_Glyph_Stroke
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Glyph_Stroke( FT_Glyph* pglyph, FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Bool destroy );
functions.description: Stroke an outline glyph using the given stroker. On success, replaces *pglyph with a new stroked glyph; optionally destroys the source glyph if destroy==1. May change glyph extents; callers may need to adjust advances.
requirements: pglyph must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid FT_Glyph handle; the referenced glyph must be an outline glyph (per docs; otherwise the call will fail).
stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker configured as desired.
destroy controls whether the input glyph is destroyed on success; the source glyph is untouched on error (per docs).
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
Callers should be prepared for increased glyph width/height due to stroke radius (per docs).

functions.name: FT_Glyph_StrokeBorder
functions.signature: FT_Error FT_Glyph_StrokeBorder( FT_Glyph* pglyph, FT_Stroker stroker, FT_Bool inside, FT_Bool destroy );
functions.description: Stroke an outline glyph using the given stroker and keep only one border: inside if inside==1, otherwise outside. On success, replaces *pglyph with the resulting glyph; optionally destroys the source glyph if destroy==1. May change glyph extents; callers may need to adjust advances.
requirements: pglyph must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid FT_Glyph handle; the referenced glyph must be an outline glyph (per docs; otherwise the call will fail).
stroker must be a valid FT_Stroker configured as desired.
inside selects the border to keep: 1 for inside, 0 for outside (per docs).
destroy controls whether the input glyph is destroyed on success; the source glyph is untouched on error (per docs).
Check the returned FT_Error; 0 means success.
Callers should be prepared for increased glyph width/height due to stroke radius (per docs).

functions.name: FT_GlyphSlot_Embolden
functions.signature: void FT_GlyphSlot_Embolden( FT_GlyphSlot slot );
functions.description: Emboldens the glyph stored in the given glyph slot by a reasonable, library-defined amount. Acts as a convenience wrapper around FT_Outline_Embolden for outline glyphs and FT_Bitmap_Embolden for bitmap glyphs. It modifies the glyph in place and increases outline/bitmap stroke weight; for outlines, height, width, and advance metrics increase by the emboldening strength (affecting even monospaced faces). Use FT_Outline_Get_CBox for precise outline bounds after the operation. Intended for quick synthetic bolding when configurable parameters aren’t needed.
requirements: slot must be a valid, non-NULL FT_GlyphSlot.
slot must contain a loaded glyph prior to the call (inferred from API usage).
The glyph must be in a format supported by the underlying routines (outline or bitmap), as this is a wrapper over FT_Outline_Embolden and FT_Bitmap_Embolden (stated).
The function mutates the glyph data in place; callers must not assume the original glyph shape/metrics remain unchanged (inferred).

Any layout that depends on glyph metrics should be recomputed after the call because metrics increase by the emboldening strength (stated for outlines; effect on bitmap metrics is not documented—unknown magnitude).

functions.name: FT_GlyphSlot_AdjustWeight
functions.signature: void FT_GlyphSlot_AdjustWeight( FT_GlyphSlot slot, FT_Fixed xdelta, FT_Fixed ydelta );
functions.description: Precisely adjusts the glyph’s weight horizontally and/or vertically by the specified deltas, expressed as fractions of the face EM size in fixed-point format (FT_Fixed, typically 16.16). Positive deltas increase weight; negative deltas decrease weight. Use to fine-tune stem thickness beyond the default embolden strength. Details about bitmap support are not documented; intended primarily for outlines based on typical FreeType conventions.
requirements: slot must be a valid, non-NULL FT_GlyphSlot.
slot must contain a loaded glyph prior to the call (inferred from API usage).
xdelta and ydelta are FT_Fixed fractions of the face EM size; use positive to increase and negative to decrease weight (stated).
At least one of xdelta or ydelta should be non-zero to have an effect (inferred).
Valid numeric range for deltas is not specified; extremely large magnitudes may produce distorted or invalid results (unknown).
Glyph format explicitly supported is not stated; based on purpose and naming, an outline glyph is expected (inferred; bitmap support unknown).

functions.name: FT_GlyphSlot_Oblique
functions.signature: void FT_GlyphSlot_Oblique( FT_GlyphSlot slot );
functions.description: Applies a right-leaning oblique (approximately 12 degrees) slant to the outline glyph stored in the given glyph slot. Modifies the outline in place to synthesize an italic-like appearance. Intended for outline glyphs.
requirements: slot must be a valid, non-NULL FT_GlyphSlot.
slot must contain a loaded outline glyph; the comment explicitly refers to outline glyphs (stated).
The function mutates the glyph outline in place; callers should not rely on the original shape after the call (inferred).
The exact slant strength is fixed (~12 degrees) and not configurable via this function (stated).

functions.name: FT_GlyphSlot_Slant
functions.signature: void FT_GlyphSlot_Slant( FT_GlyphSlot slot, FT_Fixed xslant, FT_Fixed yslant );
functions.description: Slants an outline glyph by applying a shear whose magnitude is given by the sine of an angle along the chosen axis. Provide xslant to slant along the x-axis and/or yslant to slant along the y-axis (FT_Fixed, typically 16.16). If both are non-zero, the result is a combined affine transformation. Modifies the glyph outline in place.
requirements: slot must be a valid, non-NULL FT_GlyphSlot.
slot must contain a loaded outline glyph; the comment explicitly refers to outline glyphs (stated).
xslant and yslant are FT_Fixed values representing sine of the desired slant angle along their respective axes (stated).
At least one of xslant or yslant should be non-zero to have an effect; if both are zero, the operation is a no-op (inferred).
The mathematically valid range for sine is [-1, 1] in FT_Fixed; passing values outside this range is undefined/unknown (inferred/unknown).
The function mutates the glyph outline in place; callers should not rely on the original shape after the call (inferred).

functions.name: FT_Sin
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_Sin(FT_Angle angle);
functions.description: Returns the sine of the given angle as a 16.16 fixed-point value. Angles use FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees). For computing both sine and cosine at once, prefer FT_Vector_Unit for efficiency.
requirements: angle must be an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
No error code is returned; caller should use the returned fixed-point value directly.
Behavior for extremely large input magnitudes is periodic with angle; no additional constraints stated.

functions.name: FT_Cos
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_Cos(FT_Angle angle);
functions.description: Returns the cosine of the given angle as a 16.16 fixed-point value. Angles use FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees). For computing both sine and cosine at once, prefer FT_Vector_Unit.
requirements: angle must be an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
No error code is returned; caller should use the returned fixed-point value directly.

functions.name: FT_Tan
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_Tan(FT_Angle angle);
functions.description: Returns the tangent of the given angle as a 16.16 fixed-point value. Angles use FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
requirements: angle must be an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
No error code is returned; caller should use the returned fixed-point value directly.
Returned value may be very large in magnitude near odd multiples of 90 degrees (inherent to tangent); overflow/precision limits are not documented.

functions.name: FT_Atan2
functions.signature: FT_Angle FT_Atan2(FT_Fixed x, FT_Fixed y);
functions.description: Computes the angle (arc-tangent) of the 2D vector (x, y) and returns it as an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees). This is analogous to standard atan2, determining the correct quadrant from x and y.
requirements: x and y are FT_Fixed coordinates (same units).
Return is an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
Behavior when x == 0 and y == 0 is not documented; caller should avoid passing a zero-length vector if the angle must be well-defined.

functions.name: FT_Angle_Diff
functions.signature: FT_Angle FT_Angle_Diff(FT_Angle angle1, FT_Angle angle2);
functions.description: Returns the difference angle2 - angle1, constrained to the interval (-PI, PI] in FT_Angle units (16.16 fixed-point degrees). Useful for normalized angular differences.
requirements: angle1 and angle2 must be FT_Angle values (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
Result is normalized to (-PI, PI]; no error code is returned.

functions.name: FT_Vector_Unit
functions.signature: void FT_Vector_Unit(FT_Vector* vec, FT_Angle angle);
functions.description: Writes the unit vector for the given angle to vec, setting vec->x = cos(angle) and vec->y = sin(angle). Useful to obtain both sine and cosine in one call. Angle is FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
requirements: vec must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to an FT_Vector.
angle must be an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
On success there is no return value; contents of vec are updated in place.

functions.name: FT_Vector_Rotate
functions.signature: void FT_Vector_Rotate(FT_Vector* vec, FT_Angle angle);
functions.description: Rotates the vector pointed to by vec by the given angle in place. Angle is FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
requirements: vec must be a non-NULL, writable pointer to an FT_Vector, initialized with valid coordinates.
angle must be an FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).

functions.name: FT_Vector_Length
functions.signature: FT_Fixed FT_Vector_Length(FT_Vector* vec);
functions.description: Computes and returns the Euclidean length of the vector pointed to by vec as an FT_Fixed. The length is expressed in the same units as the vector’s coordinates.
requirements: vec must be a non-NULL pointer to an FT_Vector initialized with valid coordinates.

functions.name: FT_Vector_Polarize
functions.signature: void FT_Vector_Polarize(FT_Vector* vec, FT_Fixed* length, FT_Angle* angle);
functions.description: Computes both the Euclidean length and angle of vec, writing them to length and angle respectively. The angle is returned as FT_Angle (16.16 fixed-point degrees).
